questions.stem: AWS allows users to manage their resources using a web based user interface. What is the name of this interface?

explanation.concept: The four ways to interact with AWS
explanation.correct: The AWS Management Console is the browser-based UI for creating and managing resources. The other three access methods are the CLI, the SDKs, and the underlying API — all of them programmatic rather than web-based.

distractors.A: The CLI is a command-line tool you install and run in a terminal, not a web interface.
distractors.B: The API is the HTTPS interface everything else calls underneath; it has no UI of its own.
distractors.C: SDKs are language-specific libraries (Python, Java, JavaScript) for calling AWS from your own code.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of horizontal scaling in the AWS Cloud?

options.A: Replacing an existing EC2 instance with a larger, more powerful one
options.B: Increasing the compute capacity of a single EC2 instance to address the growing demands of an application
options.C: Adding more RAM capacity to an EC2 instance
options.D: Adding more EC2 instances of the same size to handle an increase in traffic

explanation.concept: Horizontal vs vertical scaling
explanation.correct: Horizontal scaling means adding more instances of the same size — scaling out. It is the cloud-native approach because it has no upper bound and tolerates the loss of any single instance.

distractors.A: Replacing one instance with a bigger one is vertical scaling — scaling up.
distractors.B: Increasing the capacity of a single instance is vertical scaling.
distractors.C: Adding RAM to one instance is vertical scaling, and it requires a stop and restart.

questions.stem: You have noticed that several critical Amazon EC2 instances have been terminated. Which of the following AWS services would help you determine who took this action?

explanation.concept: CloudTrail answers 'who did it'; CloudWatch answers 'how is it performing'
explanation.correct: AWS CloudTrail records every API call made in the account — who made it, from which IP, and when. Terminating an EC2 instance is an API call, so CloudTrail is where you find the responsible identity.

distractors.A: Amazon Inspector scans workloads for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure; it does not log user actions.
distractors.C: Trusted Advisor gives best-practice recommendations on cost, performance, security and limits — not an audit trail.
distractors.D: The EC2 Instance Usage Report covers usage and cost data, not the identity behind an action.

questions.stem: Which of the below options are related to the reliability of AWS? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Applying the principle of least privilege to all AWS resources
options.B: Automatically provisioning new resources to meet demand
options.C: All AWS services are considered Global Services, and this design helps customers serve their international users
options.D: Providing compensation to customers if issues occur
options.E: Ability to recover quickly from failures

explanation.concept: Reliability = recovering from failure and scaling to meet demand
explanation.correct: Reliability is the ability of a workload to perform correctly and consistently, which means both recovering quickly from failures (E) and acquiring resources automatically as demand changes (B).

distractors.A: Least privilege is a security principle, not a reliability one.
distractors.C: False — most AWS services are Region-scoped. Only a handful (IAM, Route 53, CloudFront) are global.
distractors.D: Service credits exist in the SLA, but compensation is a commercial remedy, not a reliability mechanism.

questions.stem: Which statement is true regarding the AWS Shared Responsibility Model?

options.A: Responsibilities vary depending on the services used
options.B: Security of the IaaS services is the responsibility of AWS
options.C: Patching the guest OS is always the responsibility of AWS
options.D: Security of the managed services is the responsibility of the customer

explanation.concept: The responsibility line moves with the service model
explanation.correct: The split depends on the service. With EC2 (IaaS) you patch the guest OS; with S3 or Lambda the provider handles far more. AWS is always responsible for security *of* the cloud, the customer for security *in* the cloud.

distractors.B: With IaaS the customer carries most of the security burden — OS, network config, and data.
distractors.C: Guest OS patching on EC2 is the customer's responsibility, never AWS's.
distractors.D: For managed services AWS handles the underlying infrastructure and platform patching.

questions.stem: You have set up consolidated billing for several AWS accounts. One of the accounts has purchased a number of reserved instances for 3 years. Which of the following is true regarding this scenario?

options.A: The Reserved Instance discounts can only be shared with the master account
options.B: All accounts can receive the hourly cost benefit of the Reserved Instances
options.C: The purchased instances will have better performance than On-demand instances
options.D: There are no cost benefits from using consolidated billing; It is for informational purposes only

explanation.concept: Consolidated billing shares Reserved Instance benefit across the whole organization
explanation.correct: Under consolidated billing, unused Reserved Instance capacity is shared across all accounts in the organization, so any account running a matching instance can receive the discounted hourly rate.

distractors.A: The benefit is not restricted to the management account — that is the point of sharing.
distractors.C: A Reserved Instance is a billing construct. It delivers identical performance to On-Demand.
distractors.D: Consolidated billing gives real savings through volume tiering and RI sharing, not just a single invoice.

questions.stem: A company has developed an eCommerce web application in AWS. What should they do to ensure that the application has the highest level of availability?

options.A: Deploy the application across multiple Availability Zones and Edge locations
options.B: Deploy the application across multiple Availability Zones and subnets
options.C: Deploy the application across multiple Regions and Availability Zones
options.D: Deploy the application across multiple VPC’s and subnets

explanation.concept: Availability tiers: AZ < Region
explanation.correct: Multiple Availability Zones protect against a data-centre failure; multiple Regions additionally protect against an entire Region becoming unavailable. Combining both gives the highest level of availability.

distractors.A: Edge locations cache content for CloudFront — they do not run your application.
distractors.B: Subnets live inside a single AZ, so adding subnets adds no availability beyond the AZs themselves.
distractors.D: Multiple VPCs in one Region share the same Regional failure domain.

questions.stem: What does AWS Snowball provide? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Built-in computing capabilities that allow customers to process data locally
options.B: A catalog of third-party software solutions that customers need to build solutions and run their businesses
options.C: A hybrid cloud storage between on-premises environments and the AWS Cloud
options.D: An Exabyte-scale data transfer service that allows you to move extremely large amounts of data to AWS
options.E: Secure transfer of large amounts of data into and out of the AWS

explanation.concept: Snowball: physical device for bulk data transfer, with compute on board
explanation.correct: Snowball is a ruggedised physical appliance for securely moving large data sets into and out of AWS (E), and Snowball Edge variants include on-board compute so you can process data locally before shipping (A).

distractors.B: That describes AWS Marketplace.
distractors.C: Hybrid storage between on-premises and AWS is AWS Storage Gateway.
distractors.D: Exabyte-scale transfer is Snowmobile, the shipping-container service — Snowball is petabyte-scale.

questions.stem: A company has an AWS Enterprise Support plan. They want quick and efficient guidance with their billing and account inquiries. Which of the following should the company use?

explanation.concept: Concierge is the Enterprise-plan billing specialist
explanation.correct: The AWS Support Concierge is a billing and account expert included with Enterprise Support, dedicated to non-technical billing and account inquiries.

distractors.A: The AWS Health Dashboard reports service health and events affecting your resources.
distractors.C: AWS Customer Service handles billing questions for all plans, but the Enterprise-specific, faster route is Concierge.
distractors.D: There is no AWS service called Operations Support.

questions.stem: A Japanese company hosts their applications on Amazon EC2 instances in the Tokyo Region. The company has opened new branches in the United States, and the US users are complaining of high latency. What can the company do to reduce latency for the users in the US while minimizing costs?

options.A: Applying the Amazon Connect latency-based routing policy
options.B: Registering a new US domain name to serve the users in the US
options.C: Building a new data center in the US and implementing a hybrid model
options.D: Deploying new Amazon EC2 instances in a Region located in the US

explanation.concept: Latency is driven by physical distance — move the workload closer
explanation.correct: Deploying EC2 instances in a US Region places compute physically near the US users, which is the direct and low-cost way to cut latency.

distractors.A: Amazon Connect is a cloud contact-centre service and has nothing to do with routing policies.
distractors.B: A domain name does not change where the servers are, so latency is unchanged.
distractors.C: Building a data centre is the most expensive option and contradicts the cost constraint.

questions.stem: An organization has a large number of technical employees who operate their AWS Cloud infrastructure. What does AWS provide to help organize them into teams and then assign the appropriate permissions for each team?

explanation.concept: IAM groups attach permissions to a collection of users
explanation.correct: An IAM user group is a collection of IAM users that share an attached permission set — exactly the mechanism for organising employees into teams and granting each team its permissions.

distractors.A: Roles are assumed temporarily by users, applications or services; they are not a way to organise people into teams.
distractors.B: IAM users are individual identities — that is what you are trying to group.
distractors.D: AWS Organizations groups *accounts*, not users within an account.

questions.stem: A company has decided to migrate its Oracle database to AWS. Which AWS service can help achieve this without negatively impacting the functionality of the source database?

explanation.concept: DMS migrates databases while the source stays online
explanation.correct: AWS Database Migration Service keeps the source database fully operational during migration and supports continuous replication, so applications keep running throughout the move.

distractors.A: OpsWorks is managed Chef/Puppet configuration management.
distractors.C: Server Migration Service migrates whole virtual machines, not databases specifically.
distractors.D: Application Discovery Service inventories your on-premises estate to plan a migration; it does not perform one.

questions.stem: Adjusting compute capacity dynamically to reduce cost is an implementation of which AWS cloud best practice?

explanation.concept: Elasticity: match supply to demand automatically
explanation.correct: Implementing elasticity means acquiring resources when demand rises and releasing them when it falls, so you stop paying for idle capacity.

distractors.A: Security in every layer is a separate design principle about defence in depth.
distractors.B: Parallelising tasks is about throughput and concurrency, not cost-driven capacity changes.
distractors.D: AWS recommends the opposite of monolithic architecture — decoupled, loosely joined components.

questions.stem: What are the benefits of having infrastructure hosted in AWS? (Choose TWO)

options.B: There is no need to worry about security
options.C: Gaining complete control over the physical infrastructure
options.D: Operating applications on behalf of customers
options.E: All of the physical security and most of the data/network security are taken care of for you

explanation.concept: Cloud benefits: agility, and inheriting AWS's security controls
explanation.correct: Provisioning in minutes rather than weeks increases speed and agility (A), and customers inherit AWS's physical and much of its network security under the shared responsibility model (E).

distractors.B: Security is a shared responsibility — the customer still secures data, IAM and configuration.
distractors.C: Customers never get control over physical infrastructure; AWS owns and operates it.
distractors.D: AWS does not operate customer applications, except under specific managed-service engagements.

questions.stem: What is the advantage of the AWS-recommended practice of "decoupling" applications?

options.A: Allows treating an application as a single, cohesive unit
options.B: Reduces inter-dependencies so that failures do not impact other components of the application
options.C: Allows updates of any monolithic application quickly and easily
options.D: Allows tracking of any API call made to any AWS service

explanation.concept: Decoupling contains the blast radius of a failure
explanation.correct: Decoupling reduces interdependencies between components — typically via queues or load balancers — so that when one component fails or slows, the others keep working.

distractors.A: Treating an application as one cohesive unit is the monolithic approach decoupling moves away from.
distractors.C: Decoupling breaks monoliths apart rather than making them easier to update as a whole.
distractors.D: Tracking API calls is AWS CloudTrail, unrelated to architectural coupling.

questions.stem: Which of the following helps a customer view the Amazon EC2 billing activity for the past month?

explanation.concept: Cost & Usage Report is the most granular record of what you were charged
explanation.correct: AWS Cost & Usage Reports contain the most detailed billing data available, broken down by service, resource and time period — the right tool for reviewing last month's EC2 charges.

distractors.A: AWS Budgets sets thresholds and alerts on future or ongoing spend; it is not a detailed historical report.
distractors.B: The Pricing Calculator estimates the cost of a future architecture.
distractors.C: Systems Manager is for operational management of instances, not billing.

questions.stem: What do you gain from setting up consolidated billing for five different AWS accounts under another master account?

options.A: AWS services’ costs will be reduced to half the original price
options.B: The consolidated billing feature is just for organizational purpose
options.C: Each AWS account gets volume discounts
options.D: Each AWS account gets five times the free-tier services capacity

explanation.concept: Consolidated billing aggregates usage into higher volume-discount tiers
explanation.correct: Usage from all accounts is combined for pricing purposes, so the whole organization reaches volume-discount tiers sooner and every account benefits from the blended rate.

distractors.A: There is no flat 50% discount — savings come from tiering and RI sharing.
distractors.B: Consolidated billing produces genuine cost benefits, not merely organizational tidiness.
distractors.D: The AWS Free Tier applies once across the organization, not per member account.

questions.stem: What should you do in order to keep the data on EBS volumes safe? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Regularly update firmware on EBS devices
options.C: Ensure that EBS data is encrypted at rest
options.D: Store a backup daily in an external drive
options.E: Prevent any unauthorized access to AWS data centers

explanation.concept: Protect EBS data with snapshots (durability) and encryption (confidentiality)
explanation.correct: Snapshots give you point-in-time backups stored durably in S3 (B), and encryption at rest protects the data if the underlying storage were ever accessed (C).

distractors.A: Firmware on the underlying hardware is AWS's responsibility; customers have no access to it.
distractors.D: Copying data to an external drive is neither practical nor part of the AWS model.
distractors.E: Physical data-centre access control is AWS's responsibility under the shared responsibility model.

questions.stem: One of the most important AWS best-practices to follow is the cloud architecture principle of elasticity. How does this principle improve your architecture’s design?

options.A: By automatically scaling your on-premises resources based on changes in demand
options.B: By automatically scaling your AWS resources using an Elastic Load Balancer
options.C: By reducing interdependencies between application components wherever possible
options.D: By automatically provisioning the required AWS resources based on changes in demand

explanation.concept: Elasticity provisions and releases resources as demand changes
explanation.correct: Elasticity means AWS resources are automatically provisioned when demand rises and released when it falls, so capacity tracks actual load instead of a fixed guess.

distractors.A: On-premises resources are physically fixed — you cannot scale them automatically.
distractors.B: A load balancer distributes traffic across existing targets; Auto Scaling changes how many exist.
distractors.C: Reducing interdependencies is decoupling, a different design principle.

questions.stem: A startup company is operating on limited funds and is extremely concerned about cost overruns. Which of the below options can be used to notify the company when their monthly AWS bill exceeds $2000? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Setup a CloudWatch billing alarm that triggers an SNS notification when the threshold is exceeded
options.B: Configure the Amazon Simple Email Service to send billing alerts to their email address on a daily basis
options.C: Configure the AWS Budgets Service to alert the company when the threshold is exceeded
options.D: Configure AWS CloudTrail to automatically delete all AWS resources when the threshold is exceeded
options.E: Configure the Amazon Connect Service to alert the company when the threshold is exceeded

explanation.concept: Two ways to alert on spend: CloudWatch billing alarms and AWS Budgets
explanation.correct: A CloudWatch billing alarm can publish to an SNS topic when estimated charges cross a threshold (A), and AWS Budgets can alert directly on a cost threshold (C). Both are legitimate answers.

distractors.B: Amazon SES sends email you compose yourself; it has no awareness of your bill.
distractors.D: CloudTrail logs API activity and cannot delete resources — and auto-deleting resources would be catastrophic anyway.
distractors.E: Amazon Connect is a contact-centre service, unrelated to billing.

questions.stem: What does Amazon CloudFront use to distribute content to global users with low latency?

explanation.concept: Edge locations are the CloudFront caching tier
explanation.correct: CloudFront caches content at edge locations — a far larger global network than Regions or AZs — so requests are served from a point physically close to the user.

distractors.A: Global Accelerator also uses the edge network but is a separate service for TCP/UDP traffic routing.
distractors.B: Regions are where your origin infrastructure runs, not the caching tier.
distractors.D: Availability Zones are data centre clusters within a Region, not caching points.

questions.stem: What does the "Principle of Least Privilege" refer to?

options.A: You should grant your users only the permissions they need when they need them and nothing more
options.B: All IAM users should have at least the necessary permissions to access the core AWS services
options.C: All trusted IAM users should have access to any AWS service in the respective AWS account
options.D: IAM users should not be granted any permissions; to keep your account safe

explanation.concept: Least privilege: the minimum permissions, for the minimum time
explanation.correct: Least privilege means granting only the permissions required to perform a task, only when required — and removing them when no longer needed.

distractors.B: Granting access to 'the core services' by default is broader than the task requires.
distractors.C: Blanket access for trusted users is the opposite of least privilege.
distractors.D: Granting no permissions at all would make users unable to work; the principle is minimum necessary, not zero.

questions.stem: Which of the following does NOT belong to the AWS Cloud Computing models?

explanation.concept: The three cloud service models: IaaS, PaaS, SaaS
explanation.correct: Networking as a Service is not one of the three standard cloud computing models. The recognised models are IaaS, PaaS and SaaS.

distractors.A: PaaS is a standard model — you manage the application, the provider manages the platform.
distractors.B: IaaS is a standard model — you manage OS and above, the provider the hardware.
distractors.C: SaaS is a standard model — the provider manages everything, you just use the software.

questions.stem: The identification process of an online financial services company requires that new users must complete an online interview with their security team. The completed recorded interviews are only required in the event of a legal issue or a regulatory compliance breach. What is the most cost-effective service to store the recorded videos?

explanation.concept: Match the storage class to the retrieval pattern
explanation.correct: The videos are almost never retrieved and only needed for rare legal or compliance events. S3 Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost class in AWS, designed for exactly this long-term, rarely-accessed archive pattern.

distractors.A: Intelligent-Tiering suits unpredictable access patterns and costs more than Deep Archive for known-cold data.
distractors.B: AWS Marketplace is a software catalogue, not storage.
distractors.D: EBS is block storage attached to an EC2 instance — far more expensive and the wrong shape for archives.

questions.stem: Which service provides DNS in the AWS cloud?

explanation.concept: Route 53 is the DNS service (named after DNS port 53)
explanation.correct: Amazon Route 53 is the managed, highly available DNS web service, also handling domain registration and health-check-based routing policies.

distractors.B: AWS Config records and evaluates resource configuration changes for compliance.
distractors.C: CloudFront is the content delivery network.
distractors.D: Amazon EMR runs big-data frameworks such as Spark and Hadoop.

questions.stem: Hundreds of thousands of DDoS attacks are recorded every month worldwide. What service does AWS provide to help protect AWS Customers from these attacks? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: Shield handles network-layer DDoS; WAF handles application-layer attacks
explanation.correct: AWS Shield provides managed DDoS protection at layers 3 and 4 (A), and AWS WAF filters malicious HTTP/HTTPS requests at layer 7, including application-layer floods (D).

distractors.B: AWS Config tracks resource configuration changes for compliance auditing.
distractors.C: Amazon Cognito handles user sign-up, sign-in and identity federation for your applications.
distractors.E: AWS KMS manages encryption keys — it protects data, not availability.

questions.stem: A company is deploying a new two-tier web application in AWS. Where should the most frequently accessed data be stored so that the application’s response time is optimal?

explanation.concept: In-memory caching removes repeated database round trips
explanation.correct: Amazon ElastiCache holds frequently accessed data in memory (Redis or Memcached), serving it in microseconds instead of re-querying the database — the standard way to optimise response time for hot data.

distractors.A: OpsWorks is configuration management via Chef or Puppet.
distractors.B: Storage Gateway bridges on-premises storage to AWS; it adds latency rather than removing it.
distractors.C: An EBS volume is disk-based storage attached to one instance — much slower than memory and not shared.

questions.stem: You want to run a questionnaire application for only one day (without interruption), which Amazon EC2 purchase option should you use?

explanation.concept: Match the purchase option to the workload's duration and interruption tolerance
explanation.correct: On-Demand charges by the second with no commitment, which suits a short one-day workload that must not be interrupted.

distractors.A: Reserved Instances require a 1 or 3 year commitment — wasteful for one day.
distractors.B: Spot Instances can be reclaimed by AWS with two minutes' notice, violating the 'without interruption' requirement.
distractors.C: Dedicated Instances run on single-tenant hardware at a premium; there is no such isolation requirement here.

questions.stem: You are working on a project that involves creating thumbnails of millions of images. Consistent uptime is not an issue, and continuous processing is not required. Which EC2 buying option would be the most cost-effective?

explanation.concept: Spot is cheapest when the work is interruptible
explanation.correct: Thumbnail generation is fault-tolerant and does not need continuous uptime, so Spot Instances — up to 90% cheaper by using spare AWS capacity — are the most cost-effective choice.

distractors.A: Reserved Instances demand a long-term commitment for a batch job that does not run continuously.
distractors.B: On-Demand is the safe default but costs far more than Spot for interruptible work.
distractors.C: Dedicated Instances are the most expensive option and solve a compliance problem, not a cost one.

questions.stem: Which of the following can be described as a global content delivery network (CDN) service?

explanation.concept: CloudFront is the CDN
explanation.correct: Amazon CloudFront is the global content delivery network, caching content at edge locations worldwide to reduce latency for end users.

distractors.A: AWS VPN creates encrypted tunnels between your network and AWS.
distractors.B: Direct Connect is a dedicated private physical link into AWS.
distractors.C: Regions are geographic groupings of Availability Zones, not a delivery network.

questions.stem: Which of the following services allows customers to manage their agreements with AWS?

explanation.concept: Artifact is the self-service portal for AWS compliance reports and agreements
explanation.correct: AWS Artifact provides on-demand access to AWS compliance reports (such as SOC and PCI) and lets customers review, accept and manage agreements like the BAA with AWS.

distractors.B: Certificate Manager provisions and renews SSL/TLS certificates.
distractors.C: Systems Manager operates and patches your instances at scale.
distractors.D: AWS Organizations manages multiple AWS accounts and consolidated billing.

questions.stem: Which of the following are examples of AWS-Managed Services, where AWS is responsible for the operational and maintenance burdens of running the service? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: Managed services shift operational burden to AWS
explanation.correct: DynamoDB (B) and Amazon EMR (C) are managed services — AWS runs the underlying servers, patching and scaling. Your job is the data and the configuration.

distractors.A: Amazon VPC is networking you configure yourself — subnets, route tables and gateways are your responsibility.
distractors.D: IAM is a tool you use to define identities and permissions; managing those policies is entirely your responsibility.
distractors.E: EC2 is the clearest example of unmanaged infrastructure — you patch the OS and manage the instance.

questions.stem: Your company has a data store application that requires access to a NoSQL database. Which AWS database offering would meet this requirement?

explanation.concept: DynamoDB is the managed NoSQL database
explanation.correct: Amazon DynamoDB is AWS's fully managed key-value and document NoSQL database, delivering single-digit millisecond latency at any scale.

distractors.A: Aurora is a relational (SQL) database compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL.
distractors.C: EBS is block storage for EC2 instances, not a database.
distractors.D: Redshift is a relational data warehouse for analytics.

questions.stem: As part of the Enterprise support plan, who is the primary point of contact for ongoing support needs?

options.A: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) user

explanation.concept: Enterprise Support includes a designated TAM
explanation.correct: The Technical Account Manager is the designated primary point of contact on the Enterprise plan, providing proactive guidance, architectural review and coordination across AWS.

distractors.A: An IAM user is an identity in your account, not a support contact.
distractors.B: Infrastructure Event Management is a service offering for planned events, not the ongoing point of contact.
distractors.C: Consulting Partners are third-party firms, not part of the AWS support plan.

questions.stem: How can you view the distribution of AWS spending in one of your AWS accounts?

options.B: By contacting the AWS Support team
options.D: By contacting the AWS Finance team

explanation.concept: Cost Explorer visualises where the money goes
explanation.correct: AWS Cost Explorer provides graphs and filters showing spend broken down by service, account, tag and time, plus forecasting of future costs.

distractors.A: The VPC console manages networking, not billing.
distractors.B: Support can help with billing disputes, but the self-service view is Cost Explorer.
distractors.D: There is no customer-facing 'AWS Finance team' contact for this.

questions.stem: Which of the following must an IAM user provide to interact with AWS services using the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI)?

explanation.concept: Console uses passwords; CLI and SDK use access keys
explanation.correct: Programmatic access via the CLI or SDK requires an access key ID and secret access key. Username and password authenticate only to the Management Console.

distractors.B: A session token appears only with temporary credentials from STS, and never on its own.
distractors.C: A user ID is an internal identifier, not a credential you supply.
distractors.D: Username and password are for console sign-in, not the CLI.

questions.stem: You have AWS Basic support, and you have discovered that some AWS resources are being used maliciously, and those resources could potentially compromise your data. What should you do?

options.A: Contact the AWS Customer Service team

explanation.concept: The Abuse team handles misuse of AWS resources, on any support plan
explanation.correct: The AWS Trust & Safety (Abuse) team is the correct contact when AWS resources are being used maliciously. It is reachable regardless of support plan, which matters here because Basic support has no technical support.

distractors.A: Customer Service handles billing and account questions.
distractors.C: The Concierge team is an Enterprise-plan billing benefit, unavailable on Basic.
distractors.D: There is no general customer-facing 'AWS Security team' contact channel for this.

questions.stem: Select TWO examples of the AWS shared controls.

explanation.concept: Shared controls apply to both layers — AWS for infrastructure, you for the guest
explanation.correct: Patch management (A) and configuration management (D) are shared controls: AWS patches and configures the underlying infrastructure while the customer does the same for the guest OS and applications. Awareness and training is the third shared control.

distractors.B: IAM management is entirely the customer's responsibility.
distractors.C: VPC configuration is entirely the customer's responsibility.
distractors.E: Data centre operations are entirely AWS's responsibility.

questions.stem: In order to implement best practices when dealing with a “Single Point of Failure,” you should attempt to build as much automation as possible in both detecting and reacting to failure. Which of the following AWS services would help? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: ELB detects failure, Auto Scaling reacts to it
explanation.correct: An Elastic Load Balancer health-checks targets and stops routing to unhealthy ones (A), while Auto Scaling replaces failed instances and adds capacity on demand (B). Together they detect and react automatically.

distractors.C: Amazon Athena queries data in S3 with SQL — unrelated to failure handling. (The source spells it 'Athen'.)
distractors.D: Amazon ECR is a container image registry.
distractors.E: EC2 is the instance itself — a single instance is the single point of failure you are trying to eliminate.

questions.stem: A company is planning to host an educational website on AWS. Their video courses will be streamed all around the world. Which of the following AWS services will help achieve high transfer speeds?

explanation.concept: Global video delivery is a CDN problem
explanation.correct: Amazon CloudFront caches and streams the video content from edge locations near viewers worldwide, giving high transfer speeds and low latency.

distractors.A: Amazon SNS is a pub/sub notification service.
distractors.B: Kinesis Video Streams ingests live video for processing and analytics, not global course delivery.
distractors.C: CloudFormation provisions infrastructure as code.

questions.stem: A developer is planning to build a two-tier web application that has a MySQL database layer. Which of the following AWS database services would provide automated backups for the application?

options.A: A MySQL database installed on an EC2 instance

explanation.concept: Managed relational databases give you automated backups for free
explanation.correct: Amazon Aurora is a managed MySQL-compatible relational database, and like all RDS engines it provides automated backups, point-in-time recovery and patching.

distractors.A: Self-installing MySQL on EC2 makes backups entirely your responsibility.
distractors.C: DynamoDB is NoSQL and does not satisfy the MySQL requirement.
distractors.D: Neptune is a graph database, not MySQL-compatible.

questions.stem: What is the AWS service that enables AWS architects to manage infrastructure as code?

explanation.concept: CloudFormation is infrastructure as code
explanation.correct: AWS CloudFormation provisions and manages entire stacks of AWS resources from declarative JSON or YAML templates, making infrastructure versionable and repeatable.

distractors.B: AWS Config records configuration state and evaluates compliance; it does not provision resources.
distractors.C: Amazon SES sends email.
distractors.D: Amazon EMR runs big-data frameworks.

questions.stem: Under the shared responsibility model, which of the following is the responsibility of AWS?

explanation.concept: AWS owns the infrastructure; you own everything you configure on top
explanation.correct: Configuring the underlying infrastructure devices — the physical routers, switches and hosts — is AWS's responsibility as part of security *of* the cloud.

distractors.A: Client-side encryption is performed by the customer before data reaches AWS.
distractors.C: Server-side encryption is enabled and configured by the customer, even though AWS performs the operation.
distractors.D: Security Group rules are written by the customer.

questions.stem: What does the AWS Health Dashboard provide? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Detailed troubleshooting guidance to address AWS events impacting your resources
options.B: Health checks for Auto Scaling instances
options.D: A dashboard detailing vulnerabilities in your applications
options.E: Personalized view of AWS service health

explanation.concept: The Health Dashboard is about AWS-side events affecting you
explanation.correct: The AWS Health Dashboard gives a personalized view of service health for the resources you actually use (E), together with troubleshooting guidance and remediation steps for events impacting them (A).

distractors.B: Auto Scaling performs its own instance health checks; that is not part of the Health Dashboard.
distractors.C: Cost optimization recommendations come from Trusted Advisor or Cost Explorer.
distractors.D: Application vulnerability scanning is Amazon Inspector.

questions.stem: You have deployed your application on multiple Amazon EC2 instances. Your customers complain that sometimes they can’t reach your application. Which AWS service allows you to monitor the performance of your EC2 instances to assist in troubleshooting these issues?

explanation.concept: CloudWatch is the metrics and monitoring service
explanation.correct: Amazon CloudWatch collects metrics, logs and alarms for EC2 instances — CPU, network, status checks — which is what you need to diagnose intermittent reachability.

distractors.A: Lambda runs code without servers; it is not a monitoring service.
distractors.B: AWS Config tracks configuration changes, not runtime performance.
distractors.D: CloudTrail logs API calls — who did what, not how the instance is performing.

questions.stem: Your company is developing a critical web application in AWS, and the security of the application is a top priority. Which of the following AWS services will provide infrastructure security optimization recommendations?

explanation.concept: Trusted Advisor audits your account against best practices
explanation.correct: AWS Trusted Advisor inspects your environment and makes recommendations across five pillars, including security — flagging open security groups, missing MFA on the root user and exposed access keys.

distractors.A: AWS Shield defends against DDoS attacks but makes no optimization recommendations.
distractors.B: The Management Console is the UI itself, not an advisory service.
distractors.C: Secrets Manager stores and rotates credentials.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a benefit of Amazon S3? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Amazon S3 provides unlimited storage for any type of data
options.B: Amazon S3 can run any type of application or backend system
options.C: Amazon S3 stores any number of objects, but with object size limits
options.D: Amazon S3 can be scaled manually to store and retrieve any amount of data from anywhere
options.E: Amazon S3 provides 99.999999999% (11 9’s) of data durability

explanation.concept: S3 is object storage that scales automatically — it does not run code
explanation.correct: This asks which statements are NOT benefits. S3 cannot run applications or backend systems (B) — it stores objects. And S3 scales automatically rather than manually (D).

distractors.A: True — S3 offers unlimited total storage for any data type, so it is a genuine benefit.
distractors.C: True — S3 stores any number of objects, with a 5 TB limit per individual object.
distractors.E: True — S3 is designed for 99.999999999% durability.

questions.stem: In the AWS Shared responsibility Model, which of the following are the responsibility of the customer? (Choose TWO)

options.B: Controlling physical access to compute resources

explanation.concept: Customers own identity and network configuration; AWS owns the physical layer
explanation.correct: Setting password complexity rules through an IAM password policy (D) and configuring network access rules such as security groups and NACLs (E) are both squarely customer responsibilities.

distractors.A: Disk disposal and media destruction are performed by AWS in its data centres.
distractors.B: Physical access control to compute resources is AWS's responsibility.
distractors.C: Patching the underlying network infrastructure is AWS's responsibility.

questions.stem: What does AWS provide to deploy popular technologies such as IBM MQ on AWS with the least amount of effort and time?

explanation.concept: Quick Starts are pre-built reference deployments
explanation.correct: AWS Quick Start reference deployments are CloudFormation-based, expert-reviewed templates that deploy popular third-party technologies on AWS in a fraction of the usual time.

distractors.A: Aurora is a relational database service.
distractors.B: CloudWatch monitors resources.
distractors.D: OpsWorks manages configuration with Chef or Puppet — more effort, not less, for a standard product deployment.

questions.stem: An organization has decided to purchase an Amazon EC2 Reserved Instance (RI) for three years in order to reduce costs. It is possible that the application workloads could change during the reservation period. What is the EC2 Reserved Instance (RI) type that will allow the company to exchange the purchased reserved instance for another reserved instance with higher computing power if they need to?

explanation.concept: Convertible RIs trade some discount for the right to change instance attributes
explanation.correct: A Convertible Reserved Instance can be exchanged during its term for another RI with different attributes — including a larger instance type — provided the new reservation is of equal or greater value.

distractors.A: There is no 'Elastic RI' purchase type.
distractors.B: There is no 'Premium RI' purchase type.
distractors.C: Standard RIs offer the deepest discount but cannot be exchanged for a different instance family.

questions.stem: A global company with a large number of AWS accounts is seeking a way in which they can centrally manage billing and security policies across all accounts. Which AWS Service will assist them in meeting these goals?

explanation.concept: Organizations centralizes billing and policy management across many accounts
explanation.correct: AWS Organizations lets a company centrally manage billing (via consolidated billing) and enforce security/compliance policies (via Service Control Policies) across all member accounts from one management account.

distractors.B: Trusted Advisor gives account-level best-practice checks (cost, performance, security, limits) for a single account; it doesn't manage other accounts.
distractors.C: IAM User Groups organize users and permissions within one account; they can't manage billing or policy across separate AWS accounts.
distractors.D: AWS Config tracks and evaluates resource configuration compliance within an account; it has no multi-account billing or policy management role.

questions.stem: Which service provides object-level storage in AWS?

explanation.concept: Object storage (S3) vs block storage (EBS/Instance Store) vs file storage (EFS)
explanation.correct: Amazon S3 stores data as objects (data plus metadata plus key) in buckets, accessed over HTTP(S) — the definition of object-level storage in AWS.

distractors.A: Amazon EBS provides block storage volumes attached to a single EC2 instance, not object storage.
distractors.B: Instance Store is temporary block storage physically attached to the host, lost when the instance stops.
distractors.C: Amazon EFS provides file-level storage accessed via the NFS protocol, shared across multiple instances.

questions.stem: A company is concerned that they are spending money on underutilized compute resources in AWS. Which AWS feature will help ensure that their applications are automatically adding/removing EC2 compute capacity to closely match the required demand?

explanation.concept: Auto Scaling matches compute capacity to demand automatically
explanation.correct: AWS Auto Scaling monitors demand and automatically adds or removes EC2 instances to keep capacity matched to load, avoiding paying for idle, underutilized resources.

distractors.A: Elastic Load Balancer distributes incoming traffic across existing instances; it doesn't add or remove capacity itself.
distractors.B: AWS Budgets tracks and alerts on spend against a budget; it doesn't change compute capacity.
distractors.D: Cost Explorer visualizes and analyzes historical spending; it's a reporting tool, not a capacity-management feature.

questions.stem: Which S3 storage class is best for data with unpredictable access patterns?

explanation.concept: Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between tiers as access patterns change
explanation.correct: S3 Intelligent-Tiering monitors access patterns and automatically moves objects between frequent- and infrequent-access tiers, which is ideal when you don't know or can't predict how often data will be accessed.

distractors.B: Glacier Flexible Retrieval is for archival data accessed rarely, with retrieval delays — not for data with unknown access frequency.
distractors.C: S3 Standard is for frequently accessed data; choosing it assumes a known, high access pattern.
distractors.D: Standard-Infrequent Access assumes you already know access will be infrequent, which contradicts 'unpredictable'.

questions.stem: What is the AWS database service that allows you to upload data structured in key-value format?

explanation.concept: DynamoDB is AWS's managed key-value/NoSQL database
explanation.correct: Amazon DynamoDB is a NoSQL database that stores data as key-value pairs (and documents), designed for exactly this data model.

distractors.B: Aurora is a relational (SQL) database compatible with MySQL/PostgreSQL, not key-value.
distractors.C: Redshift is a relational data warehouse for analytics, using SQL and columnar storage.
distractors.D: RDS provisions relational databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL, etc.); it uses tables and SQL, not key-value structures.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding Amazon EC2 On-demand instances?

options.A: You have to pay a start-up fee when launching a new instance for the first time
options.B: The on-demand instances follow the AWS pay-as-you-go pricing model
options.C: With on-demand instances, no longer-term commitments or upfront payments are needed
options.D: When using on-demand Linux instances, you are charged per second based on an hourly rate

explanation.concept: On-Demand pricing has no upfront cost, only a pay-as-you-go rate
explanation.correct: There is no start-up fee for On-Demand instances — you simply pay the hourly (or per-second, for Linux) rate for what you use, with no upfront commitment. This statement is false, which is why it's the answer.

distractors.B: True: On-Demand follows the pay-as-you-go model, which is why it is not the incorrect statement.
distractors.C: True: On-Demand requires no long-term contract or upfront payment, unlike Reserved Instances.
distractors.D: True: On-Demand Linux instances are billed per second (minimum 60 seconds), based on an hourly rate.

questions.stem: A company has moved to AWS recently. Which of the following AWS Services will help ensure that they have the proper security settings? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: Trusted Advisor checks configuration best practices; Inspector scans for vulnerabilities
explanation.correct: AWS Trusted Advisor reviews the account against security best-practice checks (like open ports or public S3 buckets), and Amazon Inspector automatically scans EC2 instances and container images for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure — together covering proper security settings.

distractors.C: Amazon SNS is a pub/sub messaging service; it plays no role in checking security configuration.
distractors.D: Amazon CloudWatch monitors metrics, logs, and alarms for operational performance, not security posture assessment.
distractors.E: There is no AWS offering called 'Concierge Support Team' for security review — Concierge is a billing-focused role under Enterprise Support.

questions.stem: What is the AWS feature that provides an additional level of security above the default authentication mechanism of usernames and passwords?

explanation.concept: MFA adds a second authentication factor beyond username/password
explanation.correct: AWS Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) requires a second factor — a code from a hardware or virtual device — in addition to the username and password, raising the security bar above single-factor login.

distractors.A: 'Encrypted keys' isn't a named AWS authentication feature; it doesn't describe an added login factor.
distractors.B: Email verification isn't AWS's standard extra authentication mechanism for console or API sign-in.
distractors.C: AWS KMS manages encryption keys for data protection; it is unrelated to user sign-in authentication.

questions.stem: A company is introducing a new product to their customers, and is expecting a surge in traffic to their web application. As part of their Enterprise Support plan, which of the following provides the company with architectural and scaling guidance?

explanation.concept: Infrastructure Event Management is the Enterprise-plan service for launch and scaling events
explanation.correct: Infrastructure Event Management (IEM) is an Enterprise Support engagement where AWS architects review and provide guidance for planned events such as a product launch expecting a traffic surge.

distractors.A: The AWS Knowledge Center is a library of articles and FAQs, not a proactive architectural engagement.
distractors.B: The AWS Health Dashboard reports on service health and events affecting your account, not scaling guidance for a launch.
distractors.D: AWS Support Concierge handles billing and account questions, not architectural or scaling guidance.

questions.stem: You work as an on-premises MySQL DBA. The work of database configuration, backups, patching, and DR can be time-consuming and repetitive. Your company has decided to migrate to the AWS Cloud. Which of the following can help save time on database maintenance so you can focus on data architecture and performance?

explanation.concept: RDS offloads undifferentiated database administration
explanation.correct: Amazon RDS is a managed relational database service that handles provisioning, patching, backups, and disaster-recovery setup, freeing the DBA to focus on schema design and performance rather than infrastructure upkeep.

distractors.B: Redshift is a managed data warehouse for analytics, not a general-purpose relational OLTP replacement for MySQL.
distractors.C: DynamoDB is a NoSQL database; migrating a MySQL workload there means redesigning the data model, not just offloading maintenance.
distractors.D: CloudWatch is a monitoring service; it doesn't perform database backups, patching, or DR.

questions.stem: Which of the below is a best-practice when designing solutions on AWS?

options.A: Invest heavily in architecting your environment, as it is not easy to change your design later
options.B: Use AWS reservations to reduce costs when testing your production environment
options.C: Automate wherever possible to make architectural (© ) experimentation easier
options.D: Provision a large compute capacity to handle any spikes in load

explanation.concept: Automation is a core AWS design principle that reduces friction for change
explanation.correct: Automating wherever possible (infrastructure as code, automated deployments) makes it cheap and safe to experiment with and change your architecture, which is a foundational AWS Well-Architected design principle.

distractors.A: The cloud specifically enables you to change your design later; treating the initial architecture as fixed contradicts cloud design principles.
distractors.B: Reservations are a production cost-optimization tool; using them for a test environment (which should scale down or off) wastes money.
distractors.D: Provisioning large fixed capacity 'just in case' is the traditional data-center approach — the cloud principle is to scale dynamically instead.

questions.stem: According to the AWS Acceptable Use Policy, which of the following statements is true regarding penetration testing of EC2 instances?

options.A: Penetration testing is not allowed in AWS
options.B: Penetration testing is performed automatically by AWS to determine vulnerabilities in your AWS infrastructure
options.C: Penetration testing can be performed by the customer on their own instances without prior authorization from AWS
options.D: The AWS customers are only allowed to perform penetration testing on services managed by AWS

explanation.concept: AWS pre-authorizes penetration testing on a defined list of services
explanation.correct: Under the AWS Acceptable Use Policy, customers may perform penetration testing on their own instances and resources for a set of permitted services without needing prior AWS authorization, as long as they stay within the policy's rules.

distractors.A: Penetration testing is allowed for permitted services — it's not banned outright.
distractors.B: AWS doesn't automatically pen test your infrastructure for you; testing is something the customer initiates.
distractors.D: Customers can test their own resources built on AWS-managed services (within policy), not only services AWS itself manages.

questions.stem: Which service is used to ensure that messages between software components are not lost if one or more components fail?

explanation.concept: SQS decouples components with a durable message queue
explanation.correct: Amazon SQS is a managed message-queuing service that durably stores messages between producers and consumers, so if a component fails, queued messages are retained and processed once it recovers.

distractors.B: Amazon SES sends and receives email; it isn't a queuing mechanism for inter-component messages.
distractors.C: AWS Direct Connect is a dedicated network link into AWS; it doesn't durably queue or protect application messages.
distractors.D: Amazon Connect is a cloud contact-center service, unrelated to inter-component message durability.

questions.stem: The principle “design for failure and nothing will fail” is very important when designing your AWS Cloud architecture. Which of the following would help adhere to this principle? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: Design-for-failure means redundancy (AZs) plus automatic traffic rerouting (load balancing)
explanation.correct: Multiple Availability Zones (B) give physically independent, redundant infrastructure so a single facility failure doesn't take down the workload, and Elastic Load Balancing (C) automatically routes traffic away from unhealthy resources — together they implement 'design for failure'.

distractors.A: MFA is a security/authentication control, not a resilience mechanism against component failure.
distractors.D: Penetration testing finds security weaknesses; it doesn't make an architecture resilient to failure.
distractors.E: Vertical scaling makes one resource bigger, creating a single point of failure rather than removing it.

questions.stem: What is the AWS service that provides a virtual network dedicated to your AWS account?

explanation.concept: VPC is your logically isolated virtual network in AWS
explanation.correct: Amazon VPC lets you provision a logically isolated virtual network dedicated to your account, where you control IP ranges, subnets, route tables, and gateways.

distractors.A: AWS VPN provides an encrypted connection into your network; it doesn't itself define your dedicated virtual network.
distractors.B: Subnets are subdivisions within a VPC, not a standalone dedicated-network service.
distractors.C: Dedicated Hosts are physical EC2 servers dedicated to your account, unrelated to network isolation.

questions.stem: According to the AWS Shared responsibility model, which of the following are the responsibility of the customer? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Managing environmental events of AWS data centers
options.B: Protecting the confidentiality of data in transit in Amazon S3
options.C: Controlling physical access to AWS Regions
options.D: Ensuring that the underlying EC2 host is configured properly
options.E: Patching applications installed on Amazon EC2

explanation.concept: Customer owns data-in-transit protection and guest-level software
explanation.correct: Protecting the confidentiality of data in transit (B) and patching applications installed on EC2 (E) are customer responsibilities — the customer controls how data is encrypted in their application and must maintain the software they install on top of the OS.

distractors.A: Managing environmental events of AWS data centers is AWS's responsibility (security 'of' the cloud).
distractors.C: Controlling physical access to AWS Regions and data centers is exclusively AWS's job.
distractors.D: Ensuring the underlying EC2 host is configured properly is part of AWS's infrastructure responsibility, not the customer's.

questions.stem: Which of the following AWS services can be used as a compute resource? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: EC2 and Lambda are compute; VPC/CloudWatch/S3 are not
explanation.correct: Amazon EC2 (D) provides virtual server compute capacity, and AWS Lambda (E) runs code in a serverless compute model — both are compute resources.

distractors.A: Amazon VPC is networking, defining the virtual network your resources live in — not compute.
distractors.B: Amazon CloudWatch is a monitoring and observability service, not something that runs your workload.
distractors.C: Amazon S3 is object storage; it stores data, it doesn't execute code.

questions.stem: Your company is designing a new application that will store and retrieve photos and videos. Which of the following services should you recommend as the underlying storage mechanism?

explanation.concept: S3 is the default choice for durable object storage of media files
explanation.correct: Amazon S3 is purpose-built object storage for files like photos and videos, offering high durability, virtually unlimited scale, and direct HTTP access — the standard recommendation for this use case.

distractors.A: EBS is block storage attached to a single EC2 instance; it isn't designed for shareable, internet-accessible media storage.
distractors.B: SQS is a message queue, not a storage service for binary files.
distractors.D: Instance store is temporary, host-attached storage that's lost when the instance stops — unsuitable for durable media.

questions.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to a user name and password and is used to authenticate your programmatic access to AWS services and APIs?

explanation.concept: Access keys are the programmatic equivalent of a console username/password
explanation.correct: Access Keys (an access key ID and secret access key) authenticate programmatic requests to AWS APIs, CLI, and SDKs, serving the same authentication role that a username and password serve for console sign-in.

distractors.A: 'Instance Password' isn't a real AWS credential type.
distractors.B: Key pairs are used to SSH into EC2 instances, not to authenticate general AWS API calls.
distractors.D: MFA is a second factor added on top of primary credentials, not a replacement for username and password.

questions.stem: What does Amazon ElastiCache provide?

options.B: An Ehcache compatible in-memory data store
options.C: An online software store that allows Customers to launch pre-configured software with just few clicks
options.D: A domain name system in the cloud

explanation.concept: ElastiCache is a managed in-memory data store for caching
explanation.correct: Amazon ElastiCache provides managed in-memory caching (Redis or Memcached engines), which dramatically speeds up read-heavy applications by serving data from memory instead of a slower backing database.

distractors.B: ElastiCache supports Memcached and Redis, not specifically 'Ehcache'.
distractors.C: An online store for launching pre-configured software with a few clicks describes AWS Marketplace.
distractors.D: A managed DNS service describes Amazon Route 53, not ElastiCache.

questions.stem: What is the AWS service that enables you to manage all of your AWS accounts from a single master account?

explanation.concept: Organizations centralizes management of many accounts under one management account
explanation.correct: AWS Organizations lets you create and centrally manage a group of AWS accounts from a single management (formerly 'master') account, including consolidated billing and policy enforcement.

distractors.A: AWS WAF filters web traffic to protect applications; it has no multi-account management role.
distractors.B: Trusted Advisor gives best-practice recommendations for one account; it doesn't manage multiple accounts.
distractors.D: AWS Config tracks resource configuration compliance within an account, not multi-account management.

questions.stem: Which of the following EC2 instance purchasing options supports the Bring Your Own License (BYOL) model for almost every BYOL scenario?

explanation.concept: Dedicated Hosts expose the physical sockets and cores that most BYOL licensing requires
explanation.correct: Dedicated Hosts give you a physical server dedicated to your account with visibility into sockets and physical cores, which is what most existing per-socket or per-core software licenses require — making them the best fit for BYOL.

distractors.A: Dedicated Instances run on hardware dedicated to you but without the host-level visibility (sockets and cores) many BYOL licenses need.
distractors.C: On-Demand instances share underlying hardware among customers and don't expose the physical details BYOL licensing typically requires.
distractors.D: Reserved Instances are a billing discount on shared hardware, not a way to see or control the physical host for licensing.

questions.stem: Which of the following is one of the benefits of moving infrastructure from an on-premises data center to AWS?

options.A: Free support for all enterprise customers
options.D: AWS holds responsibility for managing customer applications

explanation.concept: Cloud trades capital expenditure for variable operating expenditure
explanation.correct: Moving to AWS replaces large upfront investments in data-center hardware (CapEx) with pay-as-you-go operating expenses, a core financial benefit of cloud computing.

distractors.A: Basic Support is included free for every account, but Business and Enterprise support plans are paid — support isn't free for all customers.
distractors.B: AWS provides tools for data protection, but protection isn't automatic without the customer configuring it.
distractors.D: AWS never takes over responsibility for the customer's applications — that stays with the customer under the shared responsibility model.

questions.stem: Which of the following are important design principles you should adopt when designing systems on AWS? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Always use Global Services in your architecture rather than Regional Services
options.B: Always choose to pay as you go

explanation.concept: Automate and eliminate single points of failure are core Well-Architected design principles
explanation.correct: Automating wherever possible (D) and removing single points of failure (E) are both explicit AWS design principles that make architectures more reliable and easier to evolve.

distractors.A: Global services should be used only where appropriate (e.g., IAM, Route 53); most workloads run in Regional services, so this is not a general rule.
distractors.B: Pay-as-you-go is a pricing model benefit, not itself an architectural design principle.
distractors.C: Treating servers as disposable, replaceable resources — not fixed — is the cloud-native design principle.

questions.stem: Which AWS Service can be used to establish a dedicated, private network connection between AWS and your datacenter?

explanation.concept: Direct Connect is a dedicated private network link into AWS
explanation.correct: AWS Direct Connect establishes a dedicated, private network connection from your data center to AWS, bypassing the public internet for more consistent latency and bandwidth.

distractors.B: CloudFront is a content delivery network for caching and distributing content, not a private network link.
distractors.C: AWS Snowball is a physical data-transfer device, not a persistent network connection.
distractors.D: Route 53 is DNS; it resolves names, it doesn't create a private network connection.

questions.stem: You are working on two projects that require completely different network configurations. Which AWS service or feature will allow you to isolate resources and network configurations?

explanation.concept: VPC provides isolated, per-project network boundaries
explanation.correct: A Virtual Private Cloud lets you define an isolated network with its own IP range, subnets, and routing, so two projects needing different network configurations can each get their own VPC.

distractors.A: Internet gateways connect a VPC to the internet; they don't provide isolation between separate projects.
distractors.C: Security Groups filter traffic to instances within a network; they don't create separate isolated networks.
distractors.D: CloudFront is a content delivery service, unrelated to network isolation.

questions.stem: Which of the following services can help protect your web applications from SQL injection and other vulnerabilities in your application code?

explanation.concept: WAF filters web requests against common exploits like SQL injection
explanation.correct: AWS WAF is a web application firewall that inspects HTTP(S) requests and blocks patterns matching common exploits such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting, protecting the application layer.

distractors.A: Amazon Cognito handles user sign-up and sign-in and identity federation, not request-level attack filtering.
distractors.B: AWS IAM manages permissions for AWS resources and API calls, not web application traffic inspection.
distractors.C: Aurora is a relational database engine; it doesn't filter or inspect incoming web requests.

questions.stem: An organization needs to analyze and process a large number of data sets. Which AWS service should they use?

explanation.concept: EMR runs big-data processing frameworks (Hadoop/Spark) at scale
explanation.correct: Amazon EMR is a managed big-data platform that runs frameworks like Apache Spark and Hadoop to process and analyze very large data sets.

distractors.B: Amazon MQ is a managed message broker (ActiveMQ/RabbitMQ), not a big-data analytics engine.
distractors.C: Amazon SNS is a pub/sub notification service, unrelated to large-scale data processing.
distractors.D: Amazon SQS is a message queue; it moves messages, it doesn't analyze data sets.

questions.stem: Based on the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, which of the following are the sole responsibility of AWS? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: Hardware and hypervisor layer are AWS's exclusive responsibility
explanation.correct: Creating hypervisors (C) and hardware maintenance (E) happen entirely within AWS's physical infrastructure layer, which only AWS can access and manage — customers have no role in either.

distractors.A: CloudWatch and VPC Flow Logs give the customer visibility into their own resources' network performance, so this is something the customer does, not AWS alone.
distractors.B: Installing software on EC2 instances is the customer's responsibility, since AWS only manages up to the underlying host and hypervisor.
distractors.D: Configuring ACLs (network access rules for a VPC) is a customer configuration task.

questions.stem: What is the AWS service that provides you the highest level of control over the underlying virtual infrastructure?

explanation.concept: EC2 gives OS-level IaaS control; managed services trade control for less admin burden
explanation.correct: Amazon EC2 is Infrastructure-as-a-Service — you get root or administrator access to the guest OS and can install and configure anything, giving the highest level of control among these options.

distractors.A: Redshift is a managed data warehouse; AWS manages the underlying infrastructure, limiting customer control.
distractors.B: DynamoDB is a fully managed NoSQL database with no server access at all.
distractors.D: RDS manages the underlying database engine and OS for you, trading control for reduced administration.

questions.stem: What are the default security credentials that are required to access the AWS management console for an IAM user account?

explanation.concept: Console sign-in uses a username and password by default
explanation.correct: The default credential for signing in to the AWS Management Console as an IAM user is a user name and password; MFA and access keys are additional or alternate mechanisms, not the default console requirement.

distractors.A: MFA is an optional additional factor layered on top of the username and password, not the default credential itself.
distractors.B: Security tokens are temporary credentials (e.g., from STS), not the default IAM user sign-in method.
distractors.D: Access keys authenticate programmatic (API/CLI) access, not console sign-in.

questions.stem: In your on-premises environment, you can create as many virtual servers as you need from a single template. What can you use to perform the same in AWS?

explanation.concept: An AMI is the reusable template for launching identical EC2 instances
explanation.correct: An Amazon Machine Image (AMI) packages the OS, configuration, and software needed to launch an EC2 instance, letting you create as many identical virtual servers from it as you need — the cloud equivalent of an on-premises server template.

distractors.A: IAM manages users and permissions; it has no role in defining server templates.
distractors.B: An internet gateway connects a VPC to the internet; it's unrelated to instance templates.
distractors.C: An EBS snapshot is a point-in-time backup of a volume's data, not a full instance launch template.

questions.stem: What are two advantages of using Cloud Computing over using traditional data centers? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: Cloud removes single points of failure and spreads infrastructure across facilities, unlike a single data center
explanation.correct: Eliminating single points of failure (B) is easier in the cloud thanks to multiple AZs and Regions, and AWS's distributed infrastructure (C) spans many facilities globally — both are advantages over a traditional single data center.

distractors.A: Reserved Instances do exist in AWS, but they're a billing commitment, not an advantage over a data center — the cloud advantage is elastic, on-demand capacity, not reserved capacity.
distractors.D: Virtualization exists on-premises too; it isn't unique to the cloud, so it's not a distinguishing advantage.
distractors.E: Dedicated hosting mirrors traditional single-tenant data centers; it isn't a cloud-specific advantage.

questions.stem: Which of the following aspects of security are managed by AWS? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: AWS owns hardware patching and the global physical infrastructure
explanation.correct: Hardware patching (D) of the underlying infrastructure and securing the global physical infrastructure (E) — data centers, network backbone — are entirely AWS's responsibility under the shared responsibility model.

distractors.A: Encrypting EBS volumes is a customer-configured setting, even though AWS provides the encryption capability.
distractors.B: VPC security (route tables, security groups, NACLs) is configured and managed by the customer.
distractors.C: Access permissions (IAM policies) are defined and managed by the customer, not AWS.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the operational excellence pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?

options.A: The ability of a system to recover gracefully from failure
options.B: The efficient use of computing resources to meet requirements
options.C: The ability to monitor systems and improve supporting processes and procedures
options.D: The ability to manage datacenter operations more efficiently

explanation.concept: Operational Excellence means monitoring systems and continuously improving processes
explanation.correct: The Operational Excellence pillar focuses on running and monitoring systems to deliver business value, and continually improving supporting processes and procedures.

distractors.A: Graceful recovery from failure describes the Reliability pillar.
distractors.B: Efficient use of computing resources describes the Performance Efficiency pillar.
distractors.D: Managing data-center operations isn't a Well-Architected pillar concept — AWS manages the data centers, not the customer.

questions.stem: AWS has created a large number of Edge Locations as part of its Global Infrastructure. Which of the following is NOT a benefit of using Edge Locations?

options.A: Edge locations are used by CloudFront to cache the most recent responses
options.B: Edge locations are used by CloudFront to improve your end users’ experience when uploading files
options.C: Edge locations are used by CloudFront to distribute traffic across multiple instances to reduce latency
options.D: Edge locations are used by CloudFront to distribute content to global users with low latency

explanation.concept: Edge locations cache and deliver content; they don't load-balance across instances
explanation.correct: Distributing traffic across multiple instances to reduce latency describes load balancing, not what CloudFront edge locations do — edge locations cache and deliver content close to users, so this is the false statement and the correct answer.

distractors.A: True: edge locations do cache recent CloudFront responses close to users.
distractors.B: True: CloudFront edge locations can also accelerate uploads to the origin via optimized routing.
distractors.D: True: distributing content to global users with low latency is exactly CloudFront's purpose.

questions.stem: What are the change management tools that helps AWS customers audit and monitor all resource changes in their AWS environment? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: CloudTrail logs API activity; Config tracks and evaluates resource configuration changes
explanation.correct: AWS CloudTrail (A) records every API call for auditing 'who did what', and AWS Config (E) tracks resource configuration changes over time and evaluates them against desired rules — together these are the change-management and audit tools.

distractors.B: Amazon Comprehend is a natural-language-processing AI service, unrelated to change tracking.
distractors.C: AWS Transit Gateway is a networking hub for connecting VPCs and on-premises networks, not an audit tool.
distractors.D: AWS X-Ray traces application requests for debugging performance issues, not resource configuration changes.

questions.stem: Which of the following services allows you to run containerized applications on a cluster of EC2 instances?

explanation.concept: ECS orchestrates containers on a cluster of EC2 instances (or Fargate)
explanation.correct: Amazon ECS (Elastic Container Service) runs and manages containerized applications across a cluster of EC2 instances (or serverless Fargate capacity).

distractors.B: AWS Data Pipeline orchestrates data movement and transformation jobs, not container orchestration.
distractors.C: AWS Cloud9 is a cloud-based IDE for writing and debugging code, not a container runtime.
distractors.D: AWS Personal Health Dashboard reports on events affecting your AWS resources, unrelated to running containers.

questions.stem: Which of the following services will help businesses ensure compliance in AWS?

explanation.concept: CloudTrail's audit log underpins compliance verification
explanation.correct: AWS CloudTrail logs account activity and API calls, providing the audit trail businesses need to demonstrate and verify compliance with internal and regulatory requirements.

distractors.A: CloudFront is a content delivery network; it doesn't provide an activity audit trail for compliance.
distractors.B: CloudEndure Migration replicates servers for migration and disaster recovery, unrelated to compliance auditing.
distractors.C: CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs for operational performance, not an audit log of account actions.

questions.stem: Which of the following procedures will help reduce your Amazon S3 costs?

options.A: Use the Import/Export feature to move old files automatically to Amazon Glacier
options.B: Use the right combination of storage classes based on different use cases
options.C: Pick the right Availability Zone for your S3 bucket
options.D: Move all the data stored in S3 standard to EBS

explanation.concept: Matching storage class to access pattern is the main lever for S3 cost
explanation.correct: Using the right combination of S3 storage classes (Standard, IA, Glacier, Intelligent-Tiering) based on how frequently each data set is actually accessed is the core way to reduce S3 storage costs.

distractors.A: There's no 'Import/Export' feature that auto-moves files to Glacier — that's done via S3 Lifecycle policies.
distractors.C: S3 buckets are created in a Region, not an Availability Zone, so there is no AZ selection to make that would affect cost.
distractors.D: Moving data from S3 to EBS would increase cost and complexity — EBS is more expensive, per-instance block storage, not a cost-saving move.

questions.stem: What are the AWS services/features that can help you maintain a highly available and fault-tolerant architecture in AWS? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: Auto Scaling plus load balancing keeps an architecture available despite failures or demand changes
explanation.correct: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling (B) automatically replaces unhealthy instances and adjusts capacity, and an Elastic Load Balancer (C) routes traffic only to healthy instances — together they maintain availability and fault tolerance.

distractors.A: Direct Connect provides a dedicated network link to AWS; it doesn't add redundancy or fault tolerance to the application itself.
distractors.D: CloudFormation automates resource provisioning (infrastructure as code); it doesn't itself detect failures or reroute traffic.
distractors.E: Network ACLs are stateless traffic filters for a subnet; they don't provide availability or fault tolerance.

questions.stem: Which of the following activities may help reduce your AWS monthly costs?

options.A: Enabling Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling for all of your workloads
options.B: Using the AWS Network Load Balancer (NLB) to load balance the incoming HTTP requests
options.C: Removing all of your Cost Allocation Tags
options.D: Deploying your AWS resources across multiple Availability Zones

explanation.concept: Auto Scaling avoids paying for idle capacity
explanation.correct: Enabling EC2 Auto Scaling means you only run (and pay for) the capacity actually needed at any moment, scaling down during low demand — directly reducing monthly costs.

distractors.B: NLB is a layer-4 load balancer (ALB is the layer-7 choice for HTTP traffic), and either way adding a load balancer adds cost rather than reducing it.
distractors.C: Removing Cost Allocation Tags removes your ability to track and analyze spend — it doesn't reduce actual costs.
distractors.D: Deploying across multiple AZs improves availability but adds cost (more resources running); it doesn't reduce spend.

questions.stem: What is the AWS service/feature that takes advantage of Amazon CloudFront’s globally distributed edge locations to transfer files to S3 with higher upload speeds?

explanation.concept: Transfer Acceleration routes uploads through CloudFront edge locations to S3
