explanation.correct: S3 Transfer Acceleration uses CloudFront's globally distributed edge locations as entry points, routing uploads over optimized AWS backbone network paths to speed up transfers into S3.

distractors.B: AWS WAF filters malicious web traffic; it has nothing to do with upload speed.
distractors.C: Snowmobile is a physical exabyte-scale data-transfer service (a shipping container), not an edge-location-based speed feature.
distractors.D: Snowball is a physical device for bulk offline data transfer, not an edge-location acceleration feature.

questions.stem: Which of the following AWS security features is associated with an EC2 instance and functions to filter incoming traffic requests?

explanation.concept: Security Groups are stateful, instance-level firewalls
explanation.correct: Security Groups act as a virtual firewall attached directly to an EC2 instance's network interface, filtering inbound (and outbound) traffic at the instance level.

distractors.A: AWS X-Ray traces requests through an application for debugging and performance analysis, not traffic filtering.
distractors.B: Network ACLs filter traffic at the subnet level, not attached to a specific instance.
distractors.D: VPC Flow Logs capture records of network traffic for analysis; they don't filter or block traffic.

questions.stem: Which AWS services can be used to improve the performance of a global application and reduce latency for its users? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: Global Accelerator optimizes network routing; CloudFront caches content at the edge
explanation.correct: AWS Global Accelerator (B) routes traffic over AWS's global network backbone to the optimal endpoint, and Amazon CloudFront (E) caches content at edge locations near users — both reduce latency for a global application's users.

distractors.A: AWS KMS manages encryption keys; it has no effect on network latency or performance.
distractors.C: Direct Connect provides a dedicated link from a specific on-premises location to AWS, not a general latency-reduction solution for global end users.
distractors.D: AWS Glue is a data integration and ETL service, unrelated to application latency for end users.

questions.stem: Using Amazon RDS falls under the shared responsibility model. Which of the following are customer responsibilities? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: With RDS, the customer owns the schema and data-level settings; AWS owns the engine software and OS
explanation.correct: Building the relational database schema (A) and managing database settings and parameters (C) are customer tasks — RDS is managed, but the data model and tunable settings are still the customer's to design and configure.

distractors.B: RDS performs automated backups for you; that shifts from the customer's responsibility to AWS's.
distractors.D: AWS patches the underlying database engine software for RDS as part of the managed service.
distractors.E: Installing the database software is handled by AWS when you provision an RDS instance — you don't install the engine yourself.

questions.stem: A company has a large amount of structured data stored in their on-premises data center. They are planning to migrate all the data to AWS, what is the most appropriate AWS database option?

explanation.concept: Structured, relational data maps to RDS
explanation.correct: Structured data with defined schemas and relationships fits a relational database, and Amazon RDS is AWS's managed relational database service (MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, and others), making it the appropriate migration target.

distractors.A: DynamoDB is a NoSQL key-value/document database, better suited to unstructured or flexible-schema data, not this structured relational use case.
distractors.B: Amazon SNS is a pub/sub notification service, not a database.
distractors.D: ElastiCache is an in-memory cache, not durable primary storage for structured business data.

questions.stem: A company has created a solution that helps AWS customers improve their architectures on AWS. Which AWS program may support this company?

explanation.concept: APN Consulting Partners are third-party firms that help customers build and improve on AWS
explanation.correct: AWS Partner Network (APN) Consulting Partners are professional-services firms that help customers design, migrate, and optimize their architectures on AWS — matching a company offering architecture-improvement help.

distractors.B: An AWS Technical Account Manager (TAM) is an AWS employee providing guidance to a single Enterprise Support customer, not a separate consulting company.
distractors.C: APN Technology Partners provide software products (ISV solutions) built on AWS, not architecture consulting services.
distractors.D: AWS Professional Services is AWS's own in-house consulting organization, not a third-party partner program.

questions.stem: What is the AWS serverless service that allows you to run your applications without any administrative burden?

explanation.concept: Lambda runs code without provisioning or managing servers
explanation.correct: AWS Lambda is a serverless compute service that runs your code in response to events without you provisioning, patching, or managing any servers — zero administrative burden for the compute layer.

distractors.A: Amazon Lightsail provides simplified virtual private servers; you still manage an OS instance, unlike serverless Lambda.
distractors.C: RDS instances still require you to manage database settings and instance sizing; it's a managed service but not serverless compute.
distractors.D: EC2 instances are virtual servers you must provision, patch, and manage — the opposite of serverless.

questions.stem: Jessica is managing an e-commerce web application in AWS. The application is hosted on six EC2 instances. One day, three of the instances crashed; but none of her customers were affected. What has Jessica done correctly in this scenario?

options.A: She has properly built an elastic system
options.B: She has properly built a fault tolerant system
options.C: She has properly built an encrypted system
options.D: She has properly built a scalable system

explanation.concept: Fault tolerance means the system keeps working even when components fail
explanation.correct: Because three of six instances crashed with zero customer impact, the architecture tolerated the failure and kept serving traffic — the definition of a fault-tolerant system.

distractors.A: Elasticity is about automatically adjusting capacity up or down with demand, not surviving component failure without impact.
distractors.C: Nothing in the scenario involves data encryption; encryption wasn't demonstrated here.
distractors.D: Scalability is about handling increased load, not about tolerating instance failures without customer impact.

questions.stem: Where can you store files in AWS? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: File-level storage: EFS (shared file system) and EBS (block volumes)
explanation.correct: Amazon EFS is a managed NFS file system you can mount from multiple instances, and Amazon EBS provides block volumes attached to an EC2 instance — both are places to store files.

distractors.B: SNS is a pub/sub messaging service for sending notifications between systems, not a place to store files.
distractors.D: ECS is a container orchestration service for running and scaling containers, not a storage service.
distractors.E: EMR is a managed big-data processing platform (Hadoop/Spark), not a storage service.

questions.stem: Which AWS service can be used to store and reliably deliver messages across distributed systems?

explanation.concept: SQS decouples distributed systems with durable message queues
explanation.correct: Amazon SQS is a fully managed message queuing service that reliably stores and delivers messages between decoupled application components, even if a consumer is temporarily unavailable.

distractors.B: AWS Storage Gateway connects on-premises storage to AWS cloud storage; it does not queue or deliver messages.
distractors.C: Amazon SES sends and receives email — a narrower purpose than general-purpose distributed messaging.
distractors.D: Amazon S3 is object storage for files; it has no built-in queuing or message-delivery semantics.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes the payment model that AWS makes available for customers that can commit to using Amazon EC2 over a one or 3-year term to reduce their total computing costs?

explanation.concept: Reserved Instances trade a term commitment for a discount
explanation.correct: "Save when you reserve" describes Reserved Instances: you commit to running EC2 for a one- or three-year term in exchange for a significant discount off On-Demand rates.

distractors.A: "Pay less as AWS grows" is not an AWS pricing model name; it doesn't describe a term-commitment discount.
distractors.B: "Pay as you go" describes On-Demand pricing — no commitment and no discount, the opposite of reserving.
distractors.C: "Pay less by using more" describes tiered/volume pricing (economies of scale), not a fixed-term reservation.

questions.stem: A company is migrating its on-premises database to Amazon RDS. What should the company do to ensure Amazon RDS costs are kept to a minimum?

options.C: Combine On-demand Capacity Reservations with Saving Plans

explanation.concept: Right-sizing before and after migration keeps spend matched to actual demand
explanation.correct: Right-sizing means matching instance/DB class to real workload demand both before migrating and again after, so the company isn't paying for capacity it doesn't use — a core cost-optimization practice.

distractors.B: A Multi-Region Active-Passive architecture adds standby infrastructure in a second Region for disaster recovery; it increases cost rather than minimizing it.
distractors.C: On-Demand Capacity Reservations are an EC2 construct, not applicable to RDS, and combining them with Savings Plans adds cost rather than reducing it.
distractors.D: A Multi-Region Active-Active architecture runs full capacity in two Regions simultaneously, which raises cost significantly.

questions.stem: What is the primary storage service used by Amazon RDS database instances?

explanation.concept: RDS instances sit on EBS volumes
explanation.correct: Amazon RDS database instances store their data on underlying Amazon EBS volumes, which provide the persistent block storage for the database files.

distractors.A: Glacier is a low-cost archival object storage tier; it is not attached to RDS instances as live storage.
distractors.C: EFS is a shared network file system, not the storage layer RDS instances use.
distractors.D: S3 stores RDS backups and snapshots, but it is not the primary storage for a running database instance.

questions.stem: A company is developing a new application using a microservices framework. The new application is having performance and latency issues. Which AWS Service should be used to troubleshoot these issues?

explanation.concept: X-Ray traces a request across microservices to pinpoint latency
explanation.correct: AWS X-Ray traces requests as they travel through the components of a distributed application, showing where time is spent at each hop, which pinpoints performance and latency bottlenecks.

distractors.A: CodePipeline orchestrates CI/CD release pipelines; it doesn't trace runtime request latency.
distractors.C: Amazon Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities and network exposure, not application performance.
distractors.D: CloudTrail logs API calls for auditing who did what; it doesn't trace request latency through an application.

questions.stem: Which of the following AWS services is designed with native Multi-AZ fault tolerance in mind? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: Regional services that replicate across AZs automatically
explanation.correct: Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB are Regional services that automatically replicate data across multiple Availability Zones within the Region without any customer configuration.

distractors.A: Redshift runs as a single-node or single-AZ cluster by default; multi-AZ resilience is not automatic the way it is for S3 or DynamoDB.
distractors.B: Snowball is a physical device for shipping data into and out of AWS, not an online service with built-in AZ redundancy.
distractors.D: An EBS volume lives in a single Availability Zone; achieving redundancy requires manually snapshotting or copying it elsewhere.

questions.stem: What are the Amazon RDS features that can be used to improve the availability of your database? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: Multi-AZ for failover, Read Replicas for offloading reads
explanation.correct: Multi-AZ deployment keeps a synchronous standby copy of the database in another Availability Zone for automatic failover, and Read Replicas offload read traffic and can be promoted if needed — both improve availability.

distractors.A: AWS Regions is the global infrastructure concept, not an RDS feature you enable on a database.
distractors.C: Automatic patching is a maintenance convenience; it doesn't itself protect availability during an outage.
distractors.E: Edge Locations are CloudFront/Route 53 caching points for content delivery, unrelated to RDS availability.

questions.stem: Sarah has deployed an application in the Northern California (us-west-1) region. After examining the application’s traffic, she notices that about 30% of the traffic is coming from Asia. What can she do to reduce latency for the users in Asia?

options.A: Replicate the current resources across multiple Availability Zones within the same region
options.B: Migrate the application to a hosting provider in Asia
options.D: Create a CDN using CloudFront, so that content is cached at Edge Locations close to and in Asia

explanation.concept: CloudFront caches content at edge locations near users
explanation.correct: CloudFront caches content at edge locations around the world, including in Asia, so users there are served from a nearby cache instead of round-tripping to us-west-1, cutting latency.

distractors.A: Adding Availability Zones within the same Region doesn't help users on another continent — the origin is still in California.
distractors.B: Migrating to a different hosting provider abandons AWS entirely and is a drastic, unnecessary step.
distractors.C: Recreating the website content doesn't address the geographic distance causing the latency.

questions.stem: An organization runs many systems and uses many AWS products. Which of the following services enables them to control how each developer interacts with these products?

explanation.concept: IAM governs which identities can do what
explanation.correct: AWS Identity and Access Management lets an organization create users and roles and attach policies that precisely control which actions each developer can perform on which AWS resources.

distractors.B: Amazon RDS is a managed relational database service, not an access-control tool.
distractors.C: Network ACLs filter traffic at the subnet level; they don't govern what actions a developer can take on AWS products.
distractors.D: Amazon EMR is a big-data processing service, unrelated to controlling developer access.

questions.stem: Using Amazon EC2 falls under which of the following cloud computing models?

explanation.concept: IaaS: you get raw virtualized compute and manage everything above it
explanation.correct: EC2 gives you virtual machines where you choose and manage the guest OS, runtime, and application stack yourself — the definition of Infrastructure as a Service.

distractors.A: EC2 is not SaaS at all — you configure and maintain the OS and software stack yourself, so pairing it with SaaS is wrong.
distractors.C: SaaS is a fully managed software product (like a hosted email client); EC2 requires you to manage everything above the hypervisor.
distractors.D: PaaS (like Elastic Beanstalk) manages the runtime and platform for you; EC2 leaves OS and platform management to the customer.

questions.stem: Which of the below is a best-practice when building applications on AWS?

options.A: Strengthen physical security by applying the principle of least privilege
options.B: Ensure that the application runs on hardware from trusted vendors
options.C: Use IAM policies to maintain performance
options.D: Decouple the components of the application so that they run independently

explanation.concept: Loose coupling lets components fail and scale independently
explanation.correct: Decoupling application components — for example with queues or load balancers between them — means one component's failure or scaling event doesn't cascade to the others, a core Well-Architected design principle.

distractors.A: Physical security is AWS's responsibility under the shared responsibility model, not something an application design decision addresses.
distractors.B: AWS manages the physical hardware; choosing a hardware vendor isn't a decision available to, or relevant for, an application builder.
distractors.C: IAM policies control permissions and access, not application performance.

questions.stem: Amazon Glacier is an Amazon S3 storage class that is suitable for storing [...] & [...]. (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: Glacier is built for infrequently accessed, long-lived data
explanation.correct: Glacier is a low-cost archival storage class suited to active archives kept for record-keeping and long-term analytic data sets retained for periodic analysis, both of which tolerate retrieval delay.

distractors.B: Dynamic website assets need low-latency, frequent access — S3 Standard fits that, not an archival tier.
distractors.D: Active databases require constant fast reads and writes, incompatible with archival-tier retrieval times.
distractors.E: Cached data needs millisecond access (e.g., via ElastiCache), the opposite of what an archival storage tier provides.

questions.stem: What does Amazon Elastic Beanstalk provide?

options.A: A PaaS solution to automate application deployment
options.B: A compute engine for Amazon ECS
options.C: A scalable file storage solution for use with AWS and on-premises servers

explanation.concept: Elastic Beanstalk is a PaaS: upload code, AWS handles the rest
explanation.correct: Elastic Beanstalk is a Platform as a Service offering — you upload your application code and it automatically handles provisioning, load balancing, scaling, and health monitoring.

distractors.B: Elastic Beanstalk is not a compute engine for ECS; it's its own deployment and management layer that can run on EC2.
distractors.C: Scalable file storage describes Amazon EFS, not Elastic Beanstalk.
distractors.D: A NoSQL database describes DynamoDB, unrelated to Elastic Beanstalk.

questions.stem: What is the AWS service that performs automated network assessments of Amazon EC2 instances to check for vulnerabilities?

explanation.concept: Inspector automates vulnerability scanning of EC2 workloads
explanation.correct: Amazon Inspector automatically and continuously scans EC2 instances (and container images) for known software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure.

distractors.A: Amazon Kinesis is a real-time data streaming service, unrelated to vulnerability scanning.
distractors.B: Security groups are firewalls you configure manually; they don't perform automated vulnerability assessments.
distractors.D: Network ACLs are subnet-level traffic filters you configure, not an automated scanning service.

questions.stem: Under the Shared Responsibility Model, which of the following controls do customers fully inherit from AWS? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: Inherited controls vs. shared controls in the responsibility model
explanation.correct: Environmental controls and physical controls (data center power, cooling, physical access) are entirely AWS's domain — customers inherit them fully with no action required on their part.

distractors.A: Patch management is a shared control: AWS patches the underlying infrastructure, but customers must patch their guest OS on services like EC2.
distractors.B: Database controls depend on the service — largely customer-managed unless using a fully managed database — so they aren't fully inherited.
distractors.C: Awareness & Training is a shared control: AWS trains its own staff, but customers must separately train their own employees.

questions.stem: A company needs to host a database in Amazon RDS for at least three years. Which of the following options would be the most cost-effective solution?

explanation.concept: More paid upfront on a Reserved Instance means a bigger discount
explanation.correct: Between the two Reserved Instance options offered, Partial Upfront pays a portion of the cost at the start for a lower recurring rate, yielding a larger total discount than No Upfront over the same three-year term.

distractors.A: No Upfront requires no initial payment but delivers a smaller overall discount than Partial Upfront for the same commitment length.
distractors.C: On-Demand pricing has no term discount at all, making it the most expensive option for a guaranteed three-year workload.
distractors.D: Spot Instances can be interrupted with little notice, unsuitable for a database that needs to run continuously for three years.

questions.stem: Your application has recently experienced significant global growth, and international users are complaining of high latency. What is the AWS characteristic that can help improve your international users’ experience?

explanation.concept: Global reach: Regions and edge locations close to users worldwide
explanation.correct: Global reach refers to AWS's worldwide footprint of Regions and edge locations, letting you deploy resources or cache content near users anywhere, which is what reduces latency for a growing international audience.

distractors.A: Elasticity is about scaling capacity up or down with demand; it doesn't address geographic distance from users.
distractors.C: Data durability is about not losing stored data, unrelated to network latency.
distractors.D: High availability is about uptime and resilience to failure, not about proximity to users.

questions.stem: Savings Plans are available for which of the following AWS compute services? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: Savings Plans cover flexible compute usage, not fixed instance types
explanation.correct: Savings Plans apply to flexible compute usage on Amazon EC2 and AWS Lambda (as well as Fargate) in exchange for a one- or three-year usage commitment measured in dollars-per-hour.

distractors.A: AWS Batch runs jobs on top of EC2/Fargate/ECS; it isn't itself a Savings-Plans-eligible compute category.
distractors.B: AWS Outposts has its own separate pricing model and isn't covered by Compute Savings Plans.
distractors.C: Amazon Lightsail uses its own bundled flat-rate pricing, separate from Savings Plans.

questions.stem: A company has business critical workloads hosted on AWS and they are unwilling to accept any downtime. Which of the following is a recommended best practice to protect their workloads in the event of an unexpected natural disaster?

options.A: Replicate data across multiple Edge Locations worldwide and use Amazon CloudFront to perform automatic failover in the event of an outage
options.B: Deploy AWS resources across multiple Availability Zones within the same AWS Region
options.C: Create point-in-time backups in another subnet and recover this data when a disaster occurs
options.D: Deploy AWS resources to another AWS Region and implement an Active-Active disaster recovery strategy

explanation.concept: Only a second Region protects against a regional disaster
explanation.correct: Deploying to a separate AWS Region protects against the whole primary Region becoming unavailable, and an Active-Active strategy keeps both Regions serving live traffic so failover causes zero downtime.

distractors.A: Edge locations only cache content for CloudFront; they don't run the application's backend, so they can't fail over a full workload.
distractors.B: Multiple Availability Zones protect against a data-center failure within one Region, not a Region-wide natural disaster.
distractors.C: Subnets live within the same Region, so backing up to another subnet doesn't protect against a regional disaster, and restoring from backup still incurs downtime.

questions.stem: Which statement is correct with regards to AWS service limits? (Choose TWO)

options.A: You can contact AWS support to increase the service limits
options.B: Each IAM user has the same service limit
options.C: There are no service limits on AWS
options.D: You can use the AWS Trusted Advisor to monitor your service limits
options.E: The Amazon Simple Email Service is responsible for sending email notifications when usage approaches a service limit

explanation.concept: Quotas can be raised via Support and monitored via Trusted Advisor
explanation.correct: You can request a service limit (quota) increase through AWS Support, and AWS Trusted Advisor includes checks that flag when your usage is approaching a service limit.

distractors.B: Service limits are set per account (and often per Region), not individually per IAM user.
distractors.C: Nearly every AWS service has default quotas; the claim that there are no service limits is false.
distractors.E: Amazon SES is an email-sending service; it doesn't monitor or notify about AWS service limits across the account.

questions.stem: What is the AWS tool that enables you to use scripts to manage all AWS services and resources?

explanation.concept: The CLI is the scriptable way to drive any AWS service
explanation.correct: The AWS CLI lets you script and automate calls to AWS services from a terminal, with commands that map directly onto the underlying API, so you can manage any resource from a script.

distractors.A: The AWS Console is a browser-based UI meant for manual clicking, not scripting.
distractors.B: AWS Service Catalog lets admins publish approved IT service templates for users to launch; it's not a general scripting tool.
distractors.C: AWS OpsWorks is a configuration management service built around Chef/Puppet, not a general-purpose scripting interface to all AWS services.

questions.stem: What are the connectivity options that can be used to build hybrid cloud architectures? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: Direct Connect and Site-to-Site VPN both bridge on-premises to AWS
explanation.correct: AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated private network link, and AWS Site-to-Site VPN provides an encrypted connection over the public internet — both let you connect an on-premises network to AWS to build a hybrid architecture.

distractors.A: AWS Artifact is a portal for compliance reports and agreements, not a connectivity service.
distractors.B: AWS Cloud9 is a cloud-based IDE, unrelated to network connectivity.
distractors.D: AWS CloudTrail logs API activity for auditing; it has no role in network connectivity.

questions.stem: A company has deployed a new web application on multiple Amazon EC2 instances. Which of the following should they use to ensure that the incoming HTTP traffic is distributed evenly across the instances?

explanation.concept: ALB distributes HTTP traffic at Layer 7
explanation.correct: The Application Load Balancer operates at Layer 7 and distributes incoming HTTP/HTTPS requests evenly across registered EC2 targets, with support for content-based routing rules.

distractors.A: There is no such thing as "EC2 Auto Recovery" load balancing; automatic instance recovery from CloudWatch alarms is a different, unrelated feature.
distractors.B: Auto Scaling adjusts how many instances are running based on demand; it does not itself distribute incoming traffic.
distractors.C: The Network Load Balancer operates at Layer 4 for raw TCP/UDP traffic; the Application Load Balancer is the purpose-built choice for distributing HTTP traffic with content-aware routing.

questions.stem: Which of the following AWS offerings is a MySQL-compatible relational database service that can scale capacity automatically based on demand?

explanation.concept: Aurora: MySQL/PostgreSQL-compatible with automatic storage scaling
explanation.correct: Amazon Aurora is a managed relational database compatible with MySQL (and PostgreSQL) that automatically scales storage up to large capacity and offers Aurora Serverless for automatic compute scaling based on demand.

distractors.A: Amazon Neptune is a graph database, not a relational, MySQL-compatible engine.
distractors.C: RDS for SQL Server runs the Microsoft SQL Server engine, which is not MySQL-compatible.
distractors.D: RDS for PostgreSQL is PostgreSQL-compatible, not MySQL-compatible.

questions.stem: Which of the following can help protect your EC2 instances from DDoS attacks? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: Security Groups and NACLs restrict traffic reaching an instance
explanation.correct: Security Groups filter traffic at the instance level and Network ACLs filter traffic at the subnet level; used together they restrict inbound access to only what's needed, reducing the surface exposed to DDoS traffic.

distractors.A: AWS CloudHSM is a dedicated hardware module for storing cryptographic keys, not a traffic-filtering tool.
distractors.C: AWS Batch is a batch-computing job scheduler, unrelated to network protection.
distractors.D: AWS IAM manages permissions to AWS resources; it does not filter network traffic reaching an instance.

questions.stem: What is the AWS data warehouse service that supports a high level of query performance on large amounts of datasets?

explanation.concept: Redshift: columnar, MPP data warehouse for analytical queries
explanation.correct: Amazon Redshift is a fully managed data warehouse purpose-built for fast, complex queries over large-scale structured data, using columnar storage and massively parallel processing.

distractors.B: Amazon Kinesis ingests real-time streaming data; it isn't a queryable data warehouse.
distractors.C: DynamoDB is a key-value/document NoSQL database tuned for low-latency transactional workloads, not large-scale analytical queries.
distractors.D: Amazon RDS is a general-purpose relational database for OLTP workloads, not optimized for warehouse-scale analytics.

questions.stem: Which of the following should be considered when performing a TCO analysis to compare the costs of running an application on AWS instead of on-premises?

explanation.concept: TCO weighs on-prem hardware costs against AWS's pay-as-you-go model
explanation.correct: A TCO comparison must account for the on-premises cost of physical hardware — servers, storage, networking gear, power, cooling, and facilities — against AWS's consumption-based pricing.

distractors.A: Application development cost is typically incurred whether hosted on-premises or on AWS, so it doesn't distinguish the two options' TCO.
distractors.B: Market research is unrelated to comparing infrastructure hosting costs.
distractors.C: Business analysis isn't an infrastructure cost input for a TCO comparison of hosting environments.

questions.stem: How are AWS customers billed for Linux-based Amazon EC2 usage?

options.A: EC2 instances will be billed on one second increments, with a minimum of one minute
options.B: EC2 instances will be billed on one hour increments, with a minimum of one day
options.C: EC2 instances will be billed on one minute increments, with a minimum of one hour
options.D: EC2 instances will be billed on one day increments, with a minimum of one month

explanation.concept: EC2 billing: per-second, with a 60-second minimum
explanation.correct: Linux-based (and most) On-Demand and Reserved EC2 instances are billed in one-second increments, with a minimum charge of 60 seconds.

distractors.B: Billing by the hour with a one-day minimum is far coarser than how EC2 actually bills and is incorrect.
distractors.C: Per-minute increments with a one-hour minimum described the older EC2 billing model before AWS moved to per-second billing.
distractors.D: Billing by the day with a one-month minimum is far too coarse and is not how EC2 billing works.

questions.stem: Which of the following will impact the price paid for an EC2 instance? (Choose TWO)

options.B: The Availability Zone where the instance is provisioned

explanation.concept: Instance type and location set the hourly rate
explanation.correct: The instance type (vCPU/memory/family) and the Region or Availability Zone where the instance runs both directly determine the hourly price charged for an EC2 instance.

distractors.C: Load balancing is a separate service billed independently; it doesn't change the price of the EC2 instance itself.
distractors.D: The number of S3 buckets is unrelated to EC2 instance pricing.
distractors.E: Additional private IPs on an instance's network interface don't affect its price; only certain public/Elastic IP usage carries a separate small charge.

questions.stem: A customer spent a lot of time configuring a newly deployed Amazon EC2 instance. After the workload increases, the customer decides to provision another EC2 instance with an identical configuration. How can the customer achieve this?

options.A: By creating an AWS Config template from the old instance and launching a new instance from it
options.B: By creating an EBS Snapshot of the old instance
options.C: By installing Aurora on EC2 and launching a new instance from it
options.D: By creating an AMI from the old instance and launching a new instance from it

explanation.concept: AMIs capture a full launchable copy of an instance's configuration
explanation.correct: Creating an Amazon Machine Image from the configured instance captures its OS, installed software, and settings, so new instances launched from that AMI are identical copies.

distractors.A: AWS Config tracks resource configuration compliance over time; it doesn't produce a launchable instance template.
distractors.B: An EBS snapshot only captures the attached volume's data, not a full launchable instance image with instance-level settings.
distractors.C: Aurora is a managed relational database engine; installing it on EC2 has nothing to do with replicating a generic instance's configuration.

questions.stem: A company uses AWS Organizations to manage all of its AWS accounts. Which of the following allows the company to restrict what services and actions are allowed in each individual account?

explanation.concept: SCPs set the permission ceiling across Organizations accounts
explanation.correct: Service Control Policies attach to accounts or organizational units in AWS Organizations and define the maximum permissions available, restricting which services and actions member accounts can use regardless of their local IAM policies.

distractors.A: An IAM principal is the entity making a request (a user or role), not a mechanism for restricting permissions.
distractors.C: IAM policies grant permissions within a single account but can't enforce an organization-wide restriction across all member accounts the way SCPs do.
distractors.D: AWS Fargate is a serverless compute engine for containers, unrelated to restricting account permissions.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements describes the AWS Cloud’s agility?

options.A: AWS allows you to host your applications in multiple regions around the world
options.B: AWS provides customizable hardware at the lowest possible cost
options.C: AWS allows you to provision resources in minutes
options.D: AWS allows you to pay upfront to reduce costs

explanation.concept: Agility: provisioning resources in minutes instead of weeks
explanation.correct: Agility means being able to quickly provision, spin up, and tear down resources on demand, instead of waiting weeks for physical hardware procurement — a direct benefit of the cloud's pay-as-you-go, self-service model.

distractors.A: Hosting applications in multiple Regions describes global reach, not agility.
distractors.B: Customizable hardware at the lowest cost describes an economy-of-scale cost benefit, not agility.
distractors.D: Paying upfront to reduce costs describes a commitment-based pricing strategy, not the speed of provisioning that defines agility.

questions.stem: What are the benefits of using the Amazon Relational Database Service? (Choose TWO)

options.B: Complete control over the underlying host
options.D: Scales automatically to larger or smaller instance types
options.E: Supports the document and key-value data structure

explanation.concept: RDS: managed operations plus resizable compute capacity
explanation.correct: RDS is a managed service, so AWS handles patching, backups, and provisioning, lowering the administrative burden, and you can resize the DB instance class to scale compute capacity up or down.

distractors.B: Complete control over the underlying host is the opposite of a managed service; RDS abstracts away host-level access.
distractors.D: Resizing an RDS instance class requires an explicit change (and typically a restart); it isn't automatic the way Aurora Serverless compute scaling is.
distractors.E: Support for document and key-value structures describes DynamoDB; RDS engines are relational and store tabular data.

questions.stem: What is the connectivity option that uses Internet Protocol Security (IPSec) to establish encrypted connectivity between an on-premises network and the AWS Cloud?

explanation.concept: Site-to-Site VPN: IPSec tunnel over the internet
explanation.correct: AWS Site-to-Site VPN establishes an IPSec-encrypted tunnel over the public internet between an on-premises network and a VPC.

distractors.A: An Internet Gateway lets a VPC communicate with the public internet in general; it isn't an IPSec tunnel to a specific on-premises network.
distractors.B: AWS IQ is a marketplace for hiring AWS-certified freelancers, unrelated to networking.
distractors.C: AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated private network link over physical infrastructure — it isn't an IPSec-encrypted tunnel.

questions.stem: What is the minimum level of AWS support that provides 24x7 access to technical support engineers via phone and chat?

explanation.concept: Business Support is the minimum tier with 24x7 phone/chat access
explanation.correct: Business Support is the lowest AWS Support tier that includes 24x7 access to Cloud Support Engineers via phone, chat, and email, along with faster response times.

distractors.A: Enterprise Support also includes 24x7 phone/chat but adds a Technical Account Manager and is a higher tier than the minimum needed.
distractors.B: Developer Support provides only business-hours email access to Cloud Support Associates, with no phone or chat access.
distractors.C: Basic Support is free but limited to account/billing help and documentation/forums, with no technical support by phone or chat.

questions.stem: Which of the following is used to control network traffic in AWS? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: NACLs filter at the subnet, Security Groups filter at the instance
explanation.correct: Network ACLs filter traffic at the subnet boundary (stateless), and Security Groups filter traffic at the instance/ENI level (stateful) — together these are the two mechanisms for controlling network traffic in a VPC.

distractors.B: Key Pairs authenticate SSH login to an instance; they don't filter network traffic.
distractors.C: Access Keys are credentials for programmatic API calls, unrelated to network traffic control.
distractors.D: IAM Policies control permissions to take actions on AWS resources, not the flow of network packets.

questions.stem: A company has developed a media transcoding application in AWS. The application is designed to recover quickly from hardware failures. Which one of the following types of instance would be the most cost-effective choice to use?

explanation.concept: Spot Instances suit fault-tolerant, interruptible workloads
explanation.correct: Spot Instances offer the deepest discount off On-Demand pricing and suit interruption-tolerant workloads like transcoding, which can resume on another instance if the Spot capacity is reclaimed.

distractors.A: Reserved Instances are cheaper than On-Demand but require a one- to three-year commitment, which isn't the cheapest option for a flexible, interruption-tolerant workload.
distractors.C: On-Demand pricing is flexible but the most expensive per hour, with no discount for cost-sensitive batch work.
distractors.D: Dedicated Instances run on hardware reserved for a single customer at a price premium, aimed at compliance/licensing needs rather than cost savings.

questions.stem: Which AWS Service provides the current status of all AWS Services in all AWS Regions?

explanation.concept: Service Health Dashboard reports status of every AWS service, every Region
explanation.correct: The AWS Service Health Dashboard publicly reports the current operational status of every AWS service across every AWS Region.

distractors.B: The AWS Management Console is the web UI for managing your resources, not a service-status reporting tool.
distractors.C: Amazon CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs for your own resources, not the overall health of AWS services.
distractors.D: The AWS Personal Health Dashboard shows events personalized to your own account's resources, not the global status of all AWS services.

questions.stem: Which AWS service or feature can be used to call AWS Services from different programming languages?

explanation.concept: SDKs are language-specific libraries for calling AWS from code
explanation.correct: AWS SDKs are language-specific libraries (Python, Java, JavaScript, and more) that let you call AWS service APIs directly from your application code in the language you're already using.

distractors.B: The AWS CLI is a single command-line tool, not a set of per-language libraries for embedding in application code.
distractors.C: AWS CodeDeploy automates deploying application code to compute resources; it isn't a mechanism for calling AWS APIs from code.
distractors.D: The AWS Management Console is a browser-based UI, not a programmatic interface usable from multiple programming languages.

questions.stem: Which AWS Service can be used to register a new domain name?

explanation.concept: Route 53 handles both DNS and domain registration
explanation.correct: Amazon Route 53 is AWS's DNS and domain name registration service, letting you register new domain names directly through it.

distractors.A: Amazon Personalize is a machine learning recommendation service, unrelated to domain names.
distractors.C: AWS KMS manages encryption keys, unrelated to domain registration.
distractors.D: AWS Config tracks and evaluates resource configuration compliance, unrelated to domain names.

questions.stem: App development companies move their business to AWS to reduce time-to-market and improve customer satisfaction, what are the AWS automation tools that help them deploy their applications faster? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: CloudFormation and Elastic Beanstalk automate getting apps live
explanation.correct: AWS CloudFormation automates infrastructure provisioning as code, and AWS Elastic Beanstalk automates application deployment on managed infrastructure — together they speed up getting applications from code to running.

distractors.B: AWS Migration Hub tracks the status of migrations from on-premises to AWS; it doesn't automate application deployment.
distractors.C: AWS IAM manages access and permissions, not deployment automation.
distractors.E: Amazon Macie discovers and protects sensitive data using machine learning, unrelated to deployment speed.

questions.stem: Which AWS service provides cost-optimization recommendations?

explanation.concept: Trusted Advisor gives account-wide cost-optimization checks
explanation.correct: AWS Trusted Advisor inspects your account and provides recommendations across cost optimization, performance, security, fault tolerance, and service limits.

distractors.B: The AWS Pricing Calculator estimates costs for a planned architecture before you build it; it doesn't analyze resources you've already deployed.
distractors.C: Amazon QuickSight is a business intelligence and visualization tool, not built to generate AWS cost-optimization advice.
distractors.D: AWS X-Ray traces application performance and latency, unrelated to cost optimization.

questions.stem: A company has hundreds of VPCs in multiple AWS Regions worldwide. What service does AWS offer to simplify the connection management among the VPCs?

explanation.concept: Transit Gateway replaces a VPC peering mesh with a hub
explanation.correct: AWS Transit Gateway acts as a central hub that VPCs and on-premises networks connect to, replacing a complex mesh of point-to-point peering connections with simple hub-and-spoke routing across accounts and Regions.

distractors.A: VPC Peering creates a direct one-to-one connection between two VPCs; at the scale of hundreds of VPCs this becomes an unmanageable full mesh — exactly the problem Transit Gateway solves.
distractors.C: Amazon Connect is a cloud contact-center service, unrelated to VPC networking.
distractors.D: Security Groups are instance-level firewalls, not a connectivity or routing hub between VPCs.

questions.stem: What is one benefit and one drawback of buying a reserved EC2 instance? (Select TWO)

options.A: Instances can be shut down by AWS at any time with no notification
options.B: Reserved instances require at least a one-year pricing commitment
options.C: There is no additional charge for using dedicated instances
options.D: Reserved instances provide a significant discount compared to on-demand instances
options.E: Reserved instances are best suited for periodic workloads

explanation.concept: Reserved Instances: commitment is the cost, discount is the benefit
explanation.correct: Reserved Instances require committing to at least a one-year term — the drawback, reduced flexibility — in exchange for a significant discount compared to On-Demand pricing — the benefit.

distractors.A: Being shut down by AWS with no notice describes Spot Instance interruption behavior, not Reserved Instances.
distractors.C: Dedicated Instances carry an additional premium cost rather than being free, and this is unrelated to Reserved Instance mechanics.
distractors.E: Reserved Instances suit steady-state, continuous workloads, not periodic ones — intermittent workloads are better matched to Spot or On-Demand.

questions.stem: Why does every AWS Region contain multiple Availability Zones?

options.A: Multiple Availability Zones allows you to build resilient and highly available architectures
options.B: Multiple Availability Zones results in lower total cost compared to deploying in a single Availability Zone
options.C: Multiple Availability Zones allows for data replication and global reach
options.D: Multiple Availability Zones within a region increases the storage capacity available in that region

explanation.concept: Multiple AZs let you architect around a data-center failure
explanation.correct: Each Region contains multiple, physically separate Availability Zones so you can spread resources across them and keep your application running even if one data center fails, achieving resilience and high availability.

distractors.B: Multiple AZs are about resilience, not lowering cost — running across AZs typically costs the same or more, not less.
distractors.C: Data replication for global reach describes multiple Regions and edge locations; AZs are all within a single Region.
distractors.D: AZs are separate facilities for fault isolation, not a mechanism for pooling additional storage capacity.

questions.stem: What is the most cost-effective purchasing option for running a set of EC2 instances that must always be available for a period of two months?

explanation.concept: Short, fixed-duration needs are cheapest as On-Demand
explanation.correct: For a short, fixed two-month need, On-Demand avoids the one- to three-year commitment Reserved Instances require to break even, making it the more cost-effective and appropriate choice.

distractors.B: Spot Instances can be reclaimed with short notice, unsuitable for a workload that "must always be available."
distractors.C: Reserved Instances All Upfront require a one- to three-year commitment paid upfront; over just two months you'd pay for capacity you don't use and lose that payment if you stop early.
distractors.D: Reserved Instances No Upfront still lock you into at least a one-year term, far longer than the two months needed, so you pay for unused months.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a benefit of running an application in multiple Availability Zones?

options.A: Allows you to exceed AWS service limits
options.B: Reduces application response time between servers and global users
options.D: Increases the availability of your application

explanation.concept: Multiple AZs directly raise availability by isolating failures
explanation.correct: Running an application across multiple Availability Zones means the failure of one data center doesn't take the application down, directly increasing its availability.

distractors.A: Availability Zones don't change account-level service quotas, so this doesn't let you exceed service limits.
distractors.B: Reducing response time for distant users is a latency/CDN concern, solved by edge locations or additional Regions, not by AZs that sit close together within one Region.
distractors.C: AZs are about fault isolation, not about granting extra compute capacity or quota.

questions.stem: Data security is one of the top priorities of AWS. How does AWS deal with old storage devices that have reached the end of their useful life?

options.A: AWS sells the old devices to other hosting providers
options.B: AWS destroys the old devices in accordance with industry-standard practices
options.C: AWS sends the old devices for remanufacturing
options.D: AWS stores the old devices in a secure place

explanation.concept: AWS follows documented media-sanitization procedures at end of life
explanation.correct: AWS destroys decommissioned storage devices following documented data-destruction and media-sanitization procedures, preventing any recovery of data from retired hardware.

distractors.A: Selling old devices to other hosting providers would risk exposing customer data and contradicts AWS's security commitments.
distractors.C: Remanufacturing and reusing devices without destruction would risk data leakage, not how AWS handles decommissioned media.
distractors.D: Indefinitely storing old devices isn't a documented AWS practice and doesn't itself protect data — destruction, not storage, is the control.

questions.stem: A developer needs to set up an SSL security certificate for a client's eCommerce website in order to use the HTTPS protocol. Which of the following AWS services can be used to deploy the required SSL server certificates? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: ACM issues and manages the certificate; Route 53 supplies the DNS validation ACM needs to issue it
explanation.correct: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) is the primary service for provisioning, managing, and renewing free public SSL/TLS certificates. When the domain's DNS is hosted in Amazon Route 53, ACM can add the required validation records automatically, making Route 53 part of the certificate-issuance workflow this question is testing.

distractors.C: AWS Directory Service provisions managed Microsoft Active Directory or AD Connector for identity federation — it has nothing to do with SSL certificates.
distractors.D: IAM has a legacy certificate store for uploading third-party SSL certificates in Regions where ACM isn't available, but it isn't the primary tool AWS recommends for deploying and renewing certificates today.
distractors.E: AWS Data Pipeline orchestrates data movement and transformation between compute and storage services — unrelated to certificate management.

questions.needsReview: The stored key pairs Route 53 with ACM. The more common CCP answer for this exact question pairs ACM with IAM instead (D), since IAM can also store/deploy SSL certificates for ELB/CloudFront in Regions without ACM. Route 53's role is limited to DNS validation, not certificate deployment itself.

questions.stem: Which of the following AWS services scale automatically without your intervention? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: Fully managed services auto-scale; instance/volume-based services don't without configuration
explanation.correct: Amazon S3 scales storage capacity automatically and transparently as objects are added — there's no provisioning step. AWS Lambda scales compute automatically by running one function instance per concurrent invocation, with no capacity to manage.

distractors.A: Amazon EC2 instances run at a fixed size until you resize them or attach Auto Scaling — EC2 alone does not scale itself.
distractors.D: Amazon EMR clusters scale only if you enable and configure managed scaling; the base cluster size is fixed.
distractors.E: Amazon EBS volumes have a fixed provisioned size; growing one requires an explicit modify-volume action.

questions.stem: A company is planning to migrate an application from Amazon EC2 to AWS Lambda to use a serverless architecture. Which of the following will be the responsibility of AWS after migration? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: Serverless shifts capacity and OS ownership to AWS
explanation.correct: With Lambda, AWS provisions and scales the underlying compute (capacity management) and patches and maintains the host operating system — both are handled entirely by AWS so the customer only supplies code.

distractors.A: Application management — the function's logic, configuration, and business behavior — stays with the customer even in a serverless model.
distractors.C: Access control (IAM permissions, resource policies) is defined and managed by the customer, not AWS.
distractors.E: Data management, including what data the function processes and how it's stored, remains the customer's responsibility.

questions.stem: How do ELBs improve the reliability of your application?

options.A: By distributing traffic across multiple S3 buckets
options.B: By replicating data to multiple availability zones
options.D: By ensuring that only healthy targets receive traffic

explanation.concept: ELB health checks: traffic only reaches targets that pass
explanation.correct: Elastic Load Balancers continuously run health checks against registered targets and route traffic only to the ones that report healthy, automatically removing failed instances from rotation.

distractors.A: ELBs distribute traffic across EC2 instances or other compute targets, not S3 buckets.
distractors.B: Cross-AZ data replication is handled by services like RDS or S3, not by the load balancer.
distractors.C: Creating database Read Replicas is an RDS feature, unrelated to how ELB improves reliability.

questions.stem: A company needs to migrate their website from on-premises to AWS. Security is a major concern for them, so they need to host their website on hardware that is NOT shared with other AWS customers. Which of the following EC2 instance options meets this requirement?

explanation.concept: Dedicated Instances run on hardware dedicated to a single account
explanation.correct: Dedicated Instances run on physical servers dedicated to a single AWS account, isolating you from other customers' EC2 instances at the hardware level.

distractors.A: On-Demand instances run on shared multi-tenant hardware by default.
distractors.B: Spot instances are also multi-tenant, just billed at variable spare-capacity rates.
distractors.D: Reserved Instances are a billing and capacity commitment, not a hardware isolation option; the underlying hardware is still shared unless you also select the Dedicated tenancy attribute.

questions.stem: A customer is planning to move billions of images and videos to be stored on Amazon S3. The customer has approximately 60 Petabytes of data to move. Which of the following AWS Services is the best choice to transfer the data to AWS?

explanation.concept: Scale of the transfer decides Snowball vs Snowmobile
explanation.correct: AWS Snowmobile is an exabyte-scale data transfer service delivered in a shipping container on a truck, purpose-built for multi-petabyte migrations like this 60 PB dataset.

distractors.A: Snowball devices hold tens of terabytes each; moving 60 PB with Snowball would require an impractical number of devices and shipments.
distractors.B: S3 Transfer Acceleration speeds up network uploads over the internet — at 60 PB, network transfer would still take far too long regardless of acceleration.
distractors.D: Amazon VPC is a networking construct for isolated cloud resources, not a data transfer mechanism.

questions.stem: A company plans to migrate a large amount of archived data to AWS. The archived data must be maintained for a period of 5 years and must be retrievable within 5 hours of a request. What is the most cost-effective AWS storage service to use?

explanation.concept: Glacier retrieval tiers cover hour-scale SLAs cheaply
explanation.correct: Amazon S3 Glacier is built for long-term archival at low cost, with standard retrieval typically completing within 3–5 hours — matching the 5-hour requirement far more cheaply than keeping the data in a general-purpose storage class.

distractors.B: Amazon EFS is a file system for active, frequently accessed workloads, priced well above archival storage.
distractors.C: Amazon S3 Standard is designed for frequently accessed data with millisecond retrieval, not cost-optimized for a 5-year cold archive.
distractors.D: Amazon EBS provides block storage attached to a single EC2 instance, not a durable, cost-effective long-term archive.

questions.stem: Which AWS Service is used to manage user permissions?

explanation.concept: IAM is the identity and permissions service
explanation.correct: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) is the service for creating users, groups, roles, and policies that control who can do what across AWS.

distractors.A: Security Groups are instance/ENI-level virtual firewalls that filter network traffic — not a user permissions system.
distractors.B: Amazon ECS is a container orchestration service, unrelated to permission management.
distractors.D: AWS Support provides access to support plans and cases, not identity or permissions management.

questions.stem: Which support plan includes AWS Support Concierge Service?

explanation.concept: Concierge Support is an Enterprise-only benefit
explanation.correct: The AWS Support Concierge team, focused on billing and account guidance, is included only with the Enterprise Support plan.

distractors.A: This tier doesn't include the dedicated Concierge team — that benefit is reserved for the top Enterprise plan.
distractors.B: Business Support includes full technical support and Trusted Advisor access, but not the Concierge team.
distractors.D: The entry-level plan covers only basic account and billing help, with no proactive concierge-style guidance.

questions.stem: A company needs to track resource changes using the API call history. Which AWS service can help the company achieve this goal?

explanation.concept: CloudTrail logs API calls; Config tracks resource state
explanation.correct: AWS CloudTrail records a history of every API call made against your account — who made it, when, and from where — which is exactly the audit trail this question asks for.

distractors.A: AWS Config tracks and evaluates resource configuration state and compliance over time, but it isn't the API call log itself.
distractors.B: Amazon CloudWatch monitors performance metrics and application/system events, not raw API call history.
distractors.D: AWS CloudFormation provisions and manages infrastructure as code; it doesn't record API call history.

questions.stem: What are the benefits of using an AWS-managed service? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Provides complete control over the virtual infrastructure
options.B: Allows customers to deliver new solutions faster
options.D: Eliminates the need to encrypt data
options.E: Allows developers to control all patching related activities

explanation.concept: Managed services trade operational burden for speed
explanation.correct: Managed services let teams ship new solutions faster because AWS handles the undifferentiated heavy lifting, which directly lowers operational complexity for the customer.

distractors.A: Managed services abstract away the underlying infrastructure — customers get less direct control over it, not complete control.
distractors.D: Managed services still require the customer to classify and encrypt sensitive data appropriately; encryption isn't eliminated.
distractors.E: Patching the underlying platform is exactly what AWS takes over in a managed service — customers do not control all patching.

questions.stem: Which of the following are use cases for Amazon S3? (Choose TWO)

options.B: Hosting websites that require sustained high CPU utilization
options.D: A media store for the CloudFront service
options.E: Processing data streams at any scale

explanation.concept: S3 fits static content and origin storage, not compute-heavy or streaming workloads
explanation.correct: Amazon S3 is commonly used to host static websites (HTML/CSS/JS with no server-side processing) and as the origin/media store that Amazon CloudFront pulls and caches content from.

distractors.B: Websites needing sustained high CPU utilization require compute (EC2, containers, or Lambda) to run server-side logic — S3 only stores objects.
distractors.C: S3 is object storage; cost-effective structured log and database storage is better served by purpose-built database or logging services, not by treating S3 as a database.
distractors.E: Processing data streams at scale is the job of Kinesis, not S3, which is passive storage.

questions.stem: What is the AWS’ recommendation regarding access keys?

options.A: Delete all access keys and use passwords instead
options.B: Only share them with trusted people
options.D: Save them within your application code

explanation.concept: AWS best practice: rotate credentials regularly
explanation.correct: AWS recommends rotating access keys on a regular schedule so any leaked or stale key has a limited window of usefulness.

distractors.A: Deleting all keys and using only passwords isn't the guidance — access keys remain the standard way to authenticate programmatic requests.
distractors.B: Access keys should never be shared with anyone, trusted or not — each identity should have its own credentials.
distractors.D: Hardcoding access keys in application code is explicitly discouraged; use IAM roles or environment-based credential providers instead.

questions.stem: What is the AWS IAM feature that provides an additional layer of security on top of user-name and password authentication?

explanation.concept: MFA adds a second authentication factor beyond the password
explanation.correct: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) requires a second, time-based one-time code from a device or app in addition to username and password, providing an extra layer of login security.

distractors.A: A key pair is used for SSH access to EC2 instances, not console sign-in authentication.
distractors.B: Access keys authenticate programmatic API/CLI calls, not interactive console sign-in.
distractors.C: An SDK is a code library for calling AWS services — it has no authentication-layer role.

questions.stem: What is the benefit of using an API to access AWS Services?

options.A: It improves the performance of AWS resources
options.B: It reduces the time needed to provision AWS resources
options.C: It reduces the number of developers necessary
options.D: It allows for programmatic management of AWS resources

explanation.concept: APIs enable programmatic, repeatable resource management
explanation.correct: Accessing AWS through its API — directly or via the CLI/SDK — lets you create, configure, and manage resources programmatically, which is the basis for automation and infrastructure as code.

distractors.A: Calling a service via API doesn't change the performance of the resources it creates.
distractors.B: APIs speed up how you request resources, but provisioning time is governed by the underlying service, not shaved off by the API call itself.
distractors.C: Programmatic access is a tool for developers, not a substitute that reduces headcount.

questions.stem: A company is planning to migrate a database with high read/write activity to AWS. What is the best storage option to use?

explanation.concept: Databases on EC2 need low-latency block storage
explanation.correct: Amazon EBS provides persistent, low-latency block storage attached to an EC2 instance, which is what a high-throughput database engine needs for its data files and logs.

distractors.A: AWS Storage Gateway bridges on-premises applications to cloud storage — it isn't the storage layer for a cloud-hosted database.
distractors.B: Amazon S3 is object storage with higher latency and no native file-system semantics, unsuitable as primary database storage.
distractors.D: Amazon Glacier is archival storage optimized for infrequent access, far too slow for active database read/write activity.

questions.stem: How can AWS customers track and avoid over-spending on underutilized reserved instances?

options.A: Customers can add all AWS accounts to an AWS Organization, enable Consolidated Billing, and turn off Reserved Instance sharing
options.B: Customers can use Amazon Neptune to track and analyze their usage patterns, detect underutilized reserved instances, and then sell them on the Amazon EC2 Reserved Instance Marketplace
options.C: Customers can use the AWS Budgets service to track the reserved instances usage and set up alert notifications when their utilization drops below the threshold that they define
options.D: Customers can use Amazon CloudTrail to automatically check for unused reservations and get recommendations to reduce their bill

explanation.concept: AWS Budgets tracks RI utilization and coverage, and alerts on thresholds
explanation.correct: AWS Budgets includes Reserved Instance utilization and coverage budgets that track how well reservations are being used and can send alerts when utilization drops below a defined threshold.

distractors.A: Consolidated billing shares RI benefit across accounts in an Organization but doesn't itself track or alert on utilization.
distractors.B: Amazon Neptune is a graph database service; it plays no role in cost or reservation tracking.
distractors.D: AWS CloudTrail logs API activity, not billing or Reserved Instance utilization data.

questions.stem: What is the AWS service that provides five times the performance of a standard MySQL database?

explanation.concept: Aurora: up to 5x MySQL throughput on a cloud-native relational engine
explanation.correct: Amazon Aurora is AWS's MySQL- and PostgreSQL-compatible relational database, and its MySQL-compatible edition delivers up to five times the throughput of standard MySQL running on comparable hardware.

distractors.B: Amazon Redshift is a data warehouse for analytics, not positioned as a faster MySQL replacement.
distractors.C: Amazon DynamoDB is a NoSQL key-value/document database, not benchmarked against MySQL performance.
distractors.D: Amazon Neptune is a graph database for connected-data workloads, unrelated to MySQL performance benchmarks.

questions.stem: What does AWS Service Catalog provide?

options.A: It enables customers to quickly find descriptions and use cases for AWS services
options.B: It enables customers to explore the different catalogs of AWS services
options.C: It simplifies organizing and governing commonly deployed IT services
options.D: It allows developers to deploy infrastructure on AWS using familiar programming languages

explanation.concept: Service Catalog: a curated, governed self-service IT catalog
explanation.correct: AWS Service Catalog lets organizations create and manage catalogs of approved IT services, simplifying how commonly deployed resources are organized and governed at scale.

distractors.A: Finding descriptions and use cases for AWS services generally is what AWS documentation provides, not Service Catalog.
distractors.B: Service Catalog doesn't expose a browsable catalog of AWS services — it's for organization-curated, approved deployable products.
distractors.D: Deploying infrastructure using familiar programming languages describes the AWS Cloud Development Kit (CDK), not Service Catalog.

questions.stem: For managed services like Amazon DynamoDB, which of the below is AWS responsible for? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: Managed database: AWS owns the engine and OS layer
explanation.correct: For a fully managed service like DynamoDB, AWS patches the database software and maintains the underlying operating system — the customer never touches either layer.

distractors.A: Protecting credentials — rotating and safeguarding access keys and passwords — is always the customer's responsibility.
distractors.B: Logging access activity, including configuring and reviewing CloudTrail or monitoring, is set up and owned by the customer.
distractors.E: Creating access policies, the IAM policies that govern who can access the table, is defined by the customer.

questions.stem: Which of the following AWS Services helps with planning application migration to the AWS Cloud?

explanation.concept: Discovery comes before migration: inventory on-prem workloads first
explanation.correct: AWS Application Discovery Service collects configuration, usage, and dependency data from on-premises servers, giving planners the inventory needed to build a migration plan.

distractors.A: AWS Snowball is a physical data transfer device used during migration execution, not for planning.
distractors.C: AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) moves database data during migration; it doesn't handle discovery or planning.
distractors.D: AWS Migration Hub tracks migration progress across tools; the discovery data collection itself is the job of Application Discovery Service.

questions.stem: A company is trying to analyze the costs applied to their AWS account recently. Which of the following provides them the most granular data about their AWS costs and usage?

explanation.concept: Cost and Usage Report: the most detailed billing dataset AWS offers
explanation.correct: The AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR) provides the most comprehensive and granular set of cost and usage data available, down to the hourly, resource-level, and tag-level detail, delivered to an S3 bucket.

distractors.A: An Amazon Machine Image is a template for launching EC2 instances — unrelated to cost data.
distractors.B: AWS Cost Explorer visualizes and filters cost trends but offers less granularity than the raw Cost and Usage Report data.
distractors.D: Amazon CloudWatch monitors operational metrics and logs, not billing or cost data.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the concept of an AWS region?

options.A: An AWS Region is a geographical location with a collection of Edge locations
options.B: An AWS Region is a virtual network dedicated only to a single AWS customer
options.C: An AWS Region is a geographical location with a collection of Availability Zones
options.D: An AWS Region represents the country where the AWS infrastructure exist

explanation.concept: A Region is a collection of Availability Zones
explanation.correct: An AWS Region is a physical geographic location that contains multiple isolated, redundant data centers grouped into Availability Zones.

distractors.A: A geographical area described by its edge locations is closer to the CloudFront/Global Accelerator footprint, not the definition of a Region.
distractors.B: A single-tenant virtual network describes an Amazon VPC, not a Region.
distractors.D: A Region isn't simply a country — some countries host multiple Regions, and Regions are defined by AWS's own infrastructure footprint, not national borders.

questions.stem: A company has discovered that multiple S3 buckets were deleted, but it is unclear who deleted the buckets. Which of the following can the company use to determine the identity that deleted the buckets?

explanation.concept: CloudTrail logs record the identity behind every API call, including deletes
explanation.correct: CloudTrail logs every S3 API call, including DeleteBucket, along with the calling identity, so they're the way to trace who deleted the buckets.

distractors.A: SNS logs relate to notification delivery, not API call auditing.
distractors.B: SQS logs relate to message queue operations, not who called an S3 API.
distractors.C: CloudWatch Logs stores logs applications send to it; it isn't the account-level API audit trail that CloudTrail provides.

questions.stem: Which of the following are factors in determining the appropriate database technology to use for a specific workload? (Choose TWO)

options.C: The number of reads and writes per second

explanation.concept: Choosing a database is about workload shape: throughput plus query pattern
explanation.correct: The right database depends on the workload: how many reads and writes per second it must sustain (C) and the nature of the queries it needs to run — simple key lookups, complex joins, graph traversal, and so on (D).

distractors.A: Availability Zones are an infrastructure resiliency concept, not a factor in choosing between relational, NoSQL, or graph engines.
distractors.B: Data sovereignty affects where data is stored, i.e. Region choice, not which database engine best fits the workload.
distractors.E: Software bugs are a quality and operations concern, not a database-selection criterion.

questions.stem: What are the benefits of implementing a tagging strategy for AWS resources? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Quickly identify resources that belong to a specific project
options.B: Quickly identify software solutions on AWS
options.C: Track API calls in your AWS account
options.D: Quickly identify deleted resources and their metadata
options.E: Track AWS spending across multiple resources

explanation.concept: Tags organize resources and allocate cost — they don't audit activity or track deletions
explanation.correct: Tags let you quickly identify which resources belong to a project by filtering on a shared tag, and, when enabled as cost allocation tags, let you track and break down AWS spending across resources.

distractors.B: Tags label resources you already have; they don't help discover which software solutions exist on AWS in general.
distractors.C: Tracking API calls is CloudTrail's job, not something tags provide.
distractors.D: Deleted resources and their metadata aren't tracked by tags — a resource's tags disappear along with the resource.

questions.stem: What are AWS shared controls?

options.A: Controls that are solely the responsibility of the customer based on the application they are deploying within AWS services
options.B: Controls that a customer inherits from AWS
options.C: Controls that apply to both the infrastructure layer and customer layers
options.D: Controls that the customer and AWS collaborate together upon to secure the infrastructure

explanation.concept: Shared controls: both AWS and the customer contribute, each in their own layer
explanation.correct: Shared controls are ones where AWS provides the control by managing the infrastructure, and the customer must also implement their part in how they configure and use the service — both parties collaborate to fully secure it, for example patch management or configuration management.

distractors.A: Controls that are solely the customer's responsibility are 'customer-specific' controls, a separate category from shared controls.
distractors.B: Controls fully inherited from AWS with no customer action are 'inherited' controls, distinct from shared controls.
distractors.C: Applying to both the infrastructure and customer layers describes where shared controls live, but the defining trait the question tests is the joint AWS-and-customer collaboration on the control, which is what D states directly.

questions.stem: Which design principles relate to performance efficiency in AWS? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Build multi-region architectures to better serve global customers
options.C: Implement strong Identity and Access controls

explanation.concept: Performance efficiency: go global, go serverless
explanation.correct: Building multi-Region architectures to serve global users with lower latency, and using serverless architectures to remove the operational overhead of managing servers, are both core Performance Efficiency design principles in the AWS Well-Architected Framework.

distractors.B: Applying security at all layers is a Security pillar principle, not Performance Efficiency.
distractors.C: Implementing strong identity and access controls belongs to the Security pillar.
distractors.E: Enabling audit logging is a Security and governance practice, not a Performance Efficiency principle.

questions.stem: Which of the below are responsibilities of the customer when using Amazon EC2? (Choose TWO)

options.C: Setup and operation of managed databases

explanation.concept: On EC2, the customer owns everything inside the instance
explanation.correct: With EC2, the customer is responsible for protecting the sensitive data they put on the instance and for installing and configuring any third-party software they need — the guest OS environment is theirs to manage.

distractors.B: Patching the underlying physical infrastructure and hypervisor is AWS's job, not the customer's.
distractors.C: Setup and operation of managed databases describes RDS, where AWS — not the customer — manages the database engine.
distractors.D: Maintaining consistent physical hardware components is entirely AWS's responsibility.

questions.stem: Why would an organization decide to use AWS over an on-premises data center? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: Elasticity and cost savings drive cloud adoption
explanation.correct: AWS lets organizations scale resources elastically up and down with demand, and replaces large upfront capital spend with pay-as-you-go usage, typically lowering overall cost compared to running an on-premises data center.

distractors.A: AWS doesn't provide free commercial software licenses; customers still pay for licensed software they run, whether bring-your-own-license or through the AWS Marketplace.
distractors.B: Technical support isn't free by default — beyond the free Basic plan, it's a paid tier such as Business or Enterprise.
distractors.D: On-site physical audits of AWS data centers aren't offered to customers; compliance is instead demonstrated through AWS Artifact reports.

questions.stem: Which of the following AWS services can help you perform security analysis and regulatory compliance auditing? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: Inspector finds vulnerabilities; Config tracks compliance against rules
explanation.correct: Amazon Inspector automatically scans workloads for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure, and AWS Config continuously evaluates resource configurations against rules, together covering security analysis and compliance auditing.

distractors.B: AWS Virtual Private Gateway is a VPN endpoint for connecting to a VPC, not an analysis or auditing tool.
distractors.C: AWS Batch runs batch computing jobs; it doesn't perform security or compliance analysis.
distractors.D: Amazon ECS orchestrates containers; it's a compute service, not a security or compliance tool.
