questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2)?

options.A: Amazon EC2 is considered a Serverless Web Service
options.B: Amazon EC2 eliminates the need to invest in hardware upfront
options.C: Amazon EC2 can launch as many or as few virtual servers as needed

explanation.concept: EC2 is a provisioned virtual server, the opposite of serverless
explanation.correct: EC2 requires you to launch, size, and manage virtual server instances yourself, which is the opposite of serverless — Lambda, not EC2, is AWS's serverless compute service.

distractors.B: Eliminating upfront hardware investment is a real EC2 benefit — you pay for instances as you use them instead of buying servers.
distractors.C: Launching as many or as few instances as needed is a genuine EC2 characteristic, enabled by Auto Scaling and on-demand provisioning.
distractors.D: Scalable computing capacity is a core EC2 characteristic — you can resize or add instances as demand changes.

questions.stem: What is the AWS Compute service that executes code only when triggered by events?

explanation.concept: Lambda: run code only in response to triggers, no idle servers
explanation.correct: AWS Lambda executes your code only when triggered by an event — an API call, file upload, schedule, and so on — and you pay only for the compute time consumed during execution.

distractors.B: Amazon CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs and can trigger actions via alarms, but it isn't the compute service that runs your code.
distractors.C: AWS Transit Gateway is a networking hub for connecting VPCs and on-premises networks, not a compute service.
distractors.D: Amazon EC2 runs persistent virtual servers that stay up whether or not they're handling events.

questions.stem: Both AWS and traditional IT distributors provide a wide range of virtual servers to meet their customers’ requirements. What is the name of these virtual servers in AWS?

explanation.concept: EC2 instances are AWS's virtual server offering
explanation.correct: Amazon EC2 Instances are the resizable virtual servers you launch in AWS, directly analogous to the physical or virtual servers a traditional IT distributor would provide.

distractors.A: EBS Snapshots are point-in-time backups of volumes, not the servers themselves.
distractors.B: Amazon VPC is the isolated virtual network the servers run inside, not the servers.
distractors.C: 'AWS Managed Servers' isn't an AWS service name — EC2 instances are what's actually offered.

questions.stem: What is the framework created by AWS Professional Services that helps organizations design a road map to successful cloud adoption?

explanation.concept: AWS Cloud Adoption Framework: a structured road map for cloud transformation
explanation.correct: The AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF), built by AWS Professional Services, organizes guidance across business, people, governance, platform, security, and operations perspectives to help organizations plan a successful path to the cloud.

distractors.A: AWS Secrets Manager stores and rotates secrets like database credentials — unrelated to adoption planning.
distractors.B: AWS WAF protects web applications from common exploits, not a planning framework.
distractors.D: Amazon EFS is a managed file storage service, unrelated to cloud adoption strategy.

questions.stem: TYMO Cloud Corp is looking forward to migrating their entire on-premises data center to AWS. What tool can they use to perform a cost-benefit analysis of moving to the AWS Cloud?

explanation.concept: The TCO Calculator compares on-premises cost to AWS cost
explanation.correct: The AWS TCO (Total Cost of Ownership) Calculator compares the cost of running workloads on-premises versus on AWS, which is exactly the cost-benefit analysis this migration decision needs.

distractors.A: AWS Cost Explorer analyzes and visualizes costs you're already incurring on AWS, not a pre-migration on-prem-versus-cloud comparison.
distractors.C: AWS Budgets sets spending thresholds and alerts for existing AWS usage, not a pre-migration comparison tool.
distractors.D: The AWS Pricing Calculator estimates the cost of a proposed AWS architecture but doesn't compare it against on-premises TCO the way the dedicated TCO Calculator does.

questions.stem: Which of the following activities supports the Operational Excellence pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?

options.A: Using AWS Trusted Advisor to find underutilized resources
options.B: Using AWS CloudTrail to record user activities
options.C: Using AWS CloudFormation to manage infrastructure as code
options.D: Deploying an application in multiple Availability Zones

explanation.concept: Operational Excellence: manage operations as code
explanation.correct: Using AWS CloudFormation to define and manage infrastructure as code lets teams deploy consistent, repeatable, version-controlled changes and recover quickly from failed deployments — a core Operational Excellence practice.

distractors.A: Using Trusted Advisor to find underutilized resources is primarily a Cost Optimization pillar practice.
distractors.B: Using CloudTrail to record user activity supports the Security pillar's auditability, not Operational Excellence directly.
distractors.D: Deploying across multiple Availability Zones is a Reliability pillar practice.

questions.stem: Why do many startup companies prefer AWS over traditional on-premises solutions? (Choose TWO)

options.A: AWS allows them to pay later when their business succeed
options.B: AWS can build complete data centers faster than any other Cloud provider
options.C: Using AWS, they can reduce time-to-market by focusing on business activities rather than on building and managing data centers
options.D: AWS removes the need to invest in operational expenditure
options.E: Using AWS allows companies to replace large capital expenditure with low variable costs

explanation.concept: Startups value speed to market and shifting capex to opex
explanation.correct: AWS lets startups focus engineering time on their product instead of building data centers, reducing time-to-market, and it replaces large upfront capital expenditure with low, usage-based variable costs — both classic reasons startups choose AWS.

distractors.A: AWS billing is pay-as-you-go, not deferred until a business 'succeeds' — that isn't how AWS pricing works.
distractors.B: Data center build speed relative to competitors isn't a documented AWS advantage relevant to why startups choose the cloud.
distractors.D: AWS doesn't remove operational expenditure entirely — usage-based cloud costs are themselves opex; what changes is trading capex for opex.

questions.stem: What are the benefits of using DynamoDB? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Automatically scales to meet required throughput capacity
options.B: Provides resizable instances to match the current demand
options.C: Supports both relational and non-relational data models
options.E: Supports the most popular NoSQL database engines such as CouchDB and MongoDB

explanation.concept: DynamoDB: auto-scaling NoSQL with single-digit millisecond latency
explanation.correct: DynamoDB automatically scales throughput capacity to meet demand and is built to deliver consistent single-digit millisecond response times at any scale.

distractors.B: 'Resizable instances' describes provisioned compute services like EC2 or RDS; DynamoDB is serverless and has no instances to resize.
distractors.C: DynamoDB is a NoSQL database — it doesn't support relational data models such as joins and foreign keys.
distractors.E: DynamoDB is AWS's own NoSQL engine; it doesn't run other engines such as CouchDB or MongoDB.

questions.stem: Which of the following can be used to protect data at rest on Amazon S3? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: Versioning guards against loss; permissions guard against unauthorized access
explanation.correct: S3 Versioning keeps prior copies of an object so accidental overwrites or deletions can be undone, and permissions (bucket policies, ACLs, IAM) control who can read or modify objects in the first place — together these protect data at rest.

distractors.B: Deduplication removes redundant copies of data to save space; it isn't a protection mechanism.
distractors.D: Decryption is the act of reversing encryption to read data — it exposes data rather than protecting it.
distractors.E: Conversion, such as format or transcoding changes, alters data representation and plays no role in protecting data at rest.

questions.stem: As part of the AWS Migration Acceleration Program (MAP), what does AWS provide to accelerate Enterprise adoption of AWS? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: MAP combines AWS Partners and Professional Services to accelerate migration
explanation.correct: The AWS Migration Acceleration Program pairs organizations with AWS Partners and AWS Professional Services, providing the expertise, tools, and investment that speed up large-scale enterprise migrations.

distractors.B: AWS Artifact is a compliance-reports portal, not part of MAP's migration-acceleration resources.
distractors.D: Amazon Athena is a serverless query service for data in S3, unrelated to migration programs.
distractors.E: Amazon Pinpoint is a customer engagement and messaging service, unrelated to migration acceleration.

questions.stem: AWS recommends some practices to help organizations avoid unexpected charges on their bill. Which of the following is NOT one of these practices?

options.A: Deleting unused EBS volumes after terminating an EC2instance
options.D: Releasing unused Elastic IPs after terminating an EC2instance

explanation.concept: Launch configurations don't cost anything; orphaned running or allocated resources do
explanation.correct: A launch configuration is just a template with no cost by itself, so deleting an unused one has no effect on the bill — that's why it's the one item on this list that isn't a real cost-avoidance practice.

distractors.A: Unused EBS volumes keep incurring storage charges after their instance is terminated, so deleting them is a real cost-saving practice.
distractors.C: Idle or unused Elastic Load Balancers are billed hourly whether or not they have healthy targets, so removing them saves money.
distractors.D: Elastic IPs not attached to a running instance incur an hourly charge, so releasing unused ones is a genuine cost-avoidance step.

questions.stem: What is the AWS tool that can help a company visualize their AWS spending in the last few months?

explanation.concept: Cost Explorer visualizes and forecasts historical AWS spend
explanation.correct: AWS Cost Explorer provides interactive graphs and reports to visualize, analyze, and forecast AWS costs and usage over time, including the last several months of spending.

distractors.B: The AWS Pricing Calculator estimates the cost of a planned architecture before you build it — it doesn't visualize historical spend.
distractors.C: AWS Budgets sets thresholds and alerts on spending; it isn't primarily a visualization tool for past trends.
distractors.D: AWS Consolidated Billing combines multiple accounts into a single bill; it doesn't provide the visual cost analysis Cost Explorer does.

questions.stem: When running a workload in AWS, the customer is NOT responsible for: (Select TWO)

explanation.concept: Data center operations and infrastructure security sit below the customer's line
explanation.correct: AWS operates the physical data centers and secures the underlying infrastructure — hardware, networking, and host virtualization — and both are entirely AWS's responsibility under the shared responsibility model, not the customer's.

distractors.A: Running penetration tests against permitted services is something customers can do themselves, following AWS's testing policy.
distractors.B: Reserving capacity, such as purchasing Reserved Instances or Capacity Reservations, is a customer decision about their own workloads.
distractors.D: Auditing and regulatory compliance of what the customer builds and stores in AWS remains the customer's responsibility.

questions.stem: Which AWS service can be used to send promotional text messages (SMS) to more than 200 countries worldwide?

explanation.concept: SNS handles both pub/sub notifications and SMS messaging
explanation.correct: Amazon SNS supports sending SMS text messages directly to mobile phone numbers in over 200 countries, in addition to its pub/sub notification capabilities.

distractors.A: Amazon SES sends and receives email, not SMS text messages.
distractors.B: Amazon S3 is object storage; it has no messaging capability.
distractors.D: Amazon SQS is a message queuing service for decoupling application components, not for sending SMS to end users.

questions.stem: Which of the following allows you to create new RDS instances? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: RDS instances can be created via infrastructure as code or directly through the console
explanation.correct: You can create a new RDS instance directly in the AWS Management Console's guided wizard, or declare one as a resource in an AWS CloudFormation template for repeatable, automated provisioning.

distractors.A: AWS CodeDeploy automates application code deployments to compute targets; it doesn't provision database instances.
distractors.B: AWS Quick Starts are reference deployment guides and templates for common architectures, not a standalone tool for creating an individual RDS instance.
distractors.D: AWS DMS (Database Migration Service) migrates data into an existing database target; it doesn't create the RDS instance itself.

questions.stem: One of the major advantages of using AWS is cost savings. What does AWS provide to reduce the cost of running Amazon EC2 instances?

explanation.concept: Per-second billing removes rounding waste
explanation.correct: AWS bills eligible EC2 instances by the second, with a 60-second minimum, instead of rounding up to the next hour, which directly lowers the cost of running variable, short-lived workloads.

distractors.A: AWS doesn't charge a separate monthly instance maintenance fee — pricing is usage-based, not a maintenance subscription.
distractors.B: Instance tagging is a free organizational feature, not a service that reduces compute cost.
distractors.D: There's no EC2 start-up fee — pricing is based purely on the time the instance runs, which per-second billing optimizes.

questions.stem: Which AWS Group assists customers in achieving their desired business outcomes?

explanation.concept: Professional Services: AWS experts helping customers reach business outcomes
explanation.correct: AWS Professional Services is the global team of AWS experts that helps customers plan, design, and achieve their specific business and technical outcomes on AWS.

distractors.A: The AWS Security Team focuses on securing AWS's own infrastructure and services, not consulting customers on business outcomes.
distractors.C: AWS Trusted Advisor is an automated tool giving best-practice recommendations, not a team engaging with a customer's business goals.
distractors.D: The Concierge Support team handles billing and account guidance for Enterprise Support customers, not general business-outcome consulting.

questions.stem: Which AWS service or feature is used to manage the keys used to encrypt customer data?

explanation.concept: KMS centralizes creation and management of encryption keys
explanation.correct: AWS Key Management Service (KMS) is the managed service for creating, storing, and controlling the encryption keys used to protect customer data across AWS services.

distractors.B: Service Control Policies (SCPs) set permission guardrails across an AWS Organization; they don't manage encryption keys.
distractors.C: MFA adds a second sign-in factor for authentication; it has no role in key management.
distractors.D: Amazon Macie discovers and classifies sensitive data, like PII, in S3; it doesn't manage encryption keys.

questions.stem: Which AWS Service allows customers to download AWS SOC & PCI reports?

explanation.concept: AWS Artifact: a self-service portal for compliance reports and agreements
explanation.correct: AWS Artifact is the self-service portal where customers can download AWS's compliance reports, including SOC and PCI reports, and review and accept agreements such as the BAA.

distractors.A: The AWS Well-Architected Tool reviews workload architectures against best practices; it doesn't host compliance reports.
distractors.C: AWS Glue is a data integration and ETL service, unrelated to compliance documentation.
distractors.D: Amazon Chime is a communications and video conferencing service, unrelated to compliance reports.

questions.stem: A company is using EC2 Instances to run their e-commerce site on the AWS platform. If the site becomes unavailable, the company will lose a significant amount of money for each minute the site is unavailable. Which design principle should the company use to minimize the risk of an outage?

explanation.concept: Fault tolerance keeps a system running through component failure
explanation.correct: Fault tolerance is the design principle of building redundancy in so that the failure of an individual component (an instance, an AZ) does not take the whole application down — critical when every minute of downtime costs money.

distractors.A: Least privilege is an IAM security principle about granting only the permissions needed, not an availability concept.
distractors.B: Pilot light is a disaster-recovery strategy where a minimal version of the environment runs in a second Region, ready to scale up — it is one implementation detail, not the general design principle being asked about here.
distractors.D: Multi-threading is an application-level programming technique, not an AWS architectural principle for outage resilience.

questions.stem: You decide to buy a reserved instance for a term of one year. Which option provides the largest total discount?

options.B: All reserved instance payment options provide the same discount level

explanation.concept: Reserved Instance payment options trade upfront cash for a bigger discount
explanation.correct: Paying the full amount upfront (All Upfront) gives AWS the most certainty and the customer the largest discount off the equivalent On-Demand rate, compared with partial or no upfront payment.

distractors.B: The discount level does differ by payment option — the more you pay upfront, the greater the total savings.
distractors.C: Partial Upfront reduces the hourly rate less than paying the full amount upfront.
distractors.D: No Upfront still discounts against On-Demand, but it is the smallest discount of the three options.

questions.stem: What features does AWS offer to help protect your data in the Cloud? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: Data protection in AWS: control who gets in, and scramble what they see
explanation.correct: Access control (via IAM policies) restricts who can reach a resource, and data encryption (at rest and in transit, e.g. via KMS) makes the data unreadable without the right key — together these are core data-protection features AWS provides.

distractors.B: MFA devices protect account sign-in, and AWS supports virtual and hardware MFA, but there is no distinct "physical MFA devices" data-protection feature framed this way.
distractors.D: AWS storage services are highly scalable, but none of them offer literally unlimited storage as a data-protection feature.
distractors.E: Load balancing (ELB) distributes traffic for availability and performance; it does not protect data confidentiality or integrity.

questions.stem: An AWS customer has used one Amazon Linux instance for 2 hours, 5 minutes and 9 seconds, and one CentOS instance for 4 hours, 23 minutes and 7 seconds. How much time will the customer be billed for?

options.A: 3 hours for the Linux instance and 5 hours for the CentOS instance
options.B: 2 hours, 5 minutes and 9 seconds for the Linux instance and 4 hours, 23 minutes and 7 seconds for the CentOS instance
options.C: 2 hours, 5 minutes and 9 seconds for the Linux instance and 5 hours for the CentOS instance
options.D: 3 hours for the Linux instance and 4 hours, 23 minutes and 7 seconds for the CentOS instance

questions.sourceExplanation:
Explanation:
- Pricing is per instance-hour consumed for each instance, from the time an instance is launched until it is terminated or stopped.
- Each partial instance-hour consumed will be billed per-second for Linux, Windows, Windows with SQL Enterprise, Windows with SQL Standard, and Windows with SQL Web Instances, and as a full hour for all other instance types.

explanation.concept: EC2 billing granularity depends on the OS
explanation.correct: Amazon Linux and most Linux distributions bill per-second (with a one-minute minimum), so the exact 2h 5m 9s is what's billed. Windows and other licensed/hourly-billed OSes like some CentOS AMI listings round up to the next full hour, so 4h 23m 7s becomes 5 hours.

distractors.A: Rounding the Linux instance up to 3 hours is wrong — per-second billing means Linux is charged for the exact duration used, not rounded up.
distractors.B: Charging the exact duration for both instances ignores that hourly-billed AMIs round up to the next full hour.
distractors.D: Rounding the Linux instance up to 3 hours is incorrect for per-second billing; only the CentOS instance rounds up here.

questions.stem: What is the AWS Support feature that allows customers to manage support cases programmatically?

explanation.concept: AWS Support API lets you manage cases programmatically
explanation.correct: The AWS Support API exposes operations to create, update, and resolve support cases and to check service health, letting customers integrate support case management into their own tools instead of using the console.

distractors.A: AWS Trusted Advisor gives automated best-practice checks across cost, performance, security, and limits — it doesn't manage support cases.
distractors.B: "AWS Operations Support" is not an AWS service name.
distractors.D: AWS Personal Health Dashboard shows the status of AWS events affecting your specific resources, not a way to open or manage support cases.

questions.stem: Which methods can be used by customers to interact with AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: IAM can be driven through the console, CLI, or SDKs
explanation.correct: The AWS CLI and AWS SDKs both let customers create and manage IAM users, roles, and policies programmatically, in addition to the Management Console.

distractors.B: Security Groups are EC2/VPC instance-level firewalls, not a way to interact with IAM.
distractors.D: Network ACLs are subnet-level firewalls in a VPC, unrelated to managing IAM identities.
distractors.E: AWS CodeCommit is a managed Git source-control service; it has no role in interacting with IAM.

questions.stem: Which of the following are types of AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) identities? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: IAM identities vs. IAM tools/attachments
explanation.correct: IAM Roles and IAM Users are the two identity types IAM provides (alongside groups) — a role is an identity assumable temporarily, a user is a persistent named identity.

distractors.A: AWS Resource Groups organize resources for management/tagging purposes; they are not an IAM identity type.
distractors.B: IAM Policies are permission documents attached to identities — they define what an identity can do, but a policy is not itself an identity.
distractors.E: AWS Organizations manages multiple AWS accounts as a hierarchy; an organization is not an IAM identity.

questions.stem: Which of the following Amazon RDS features facilitates offloading of database read activity?

explanation.concept: Read Replicas offload read traffic from the primary database
explanation.correct: RDS Read Replicas are asynchronously-updated copies of the primary database that applications can direct read-only queries to, reducing load on the primary and improving read scalability.

distractors.A: Database snapshots are point-in-time backups used for restore, not for offloading live read traffic.
distractors.B: Multi-AZ deployments provide a synchronously replicated standby for failover/high availability; the standby is not used for serving read traffic in standard Multi-AZ.
distractors.C: Automated backups create recovery points for restoring the database; they don't serve live queries.

questions.stem: How does AWS notify customers about security and privacy events pertaining to AWS services?

explanation.concept: AWS Security Bulletins are the channel for security/privacy event notices
explanation.correct: AWS publishes Security Bulletins on the AWS Security Center to notify customers about vulnerabilities and security/privacy events affecting AWS services.

distractors.A: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) issues and manages SSL/TLS certificates; it is not a notification channel.
distractors.C: The Management Console is where you operate resources, not where AWS pushes formal security notices.
distractors.D: AWS compliance resources (reports, certifications via Artifact) document AWS's compliance posture; they are not the notification mechanism for security events.

questions.stem: Which IAM entity can best be used to grant temporary access to your AWS resources?

explanation.concept: IAM Roles provide temporary, assumable credentials
explanation.correct: IAM Roles are assumed temporarily and issue short-lived credentials via AWS STS, making them the right mechanism for granting temporary access instead of permanent, long-lived credentials.

distractors.A: IAM Users have persistent, long-term credentials meant for people or applications with ongoing access needs, not temporary access.
distractors.B: A key pair is used for SSH access to EC2 instances, not for granting scoped AWS API access.
distractors.D: IAM Groups are collections of users sharing permissions; they don't grant temporary access themselves.

questions.stem: A company has a web application that is hosted on a single EC2 instance and is approaching 100 percent CPU Utilization during peak loads. Rather than scaling the server vertically, the company has decided to deploy three Amazon EC2 instances in parallel and to distribute traffic across the three servers. What AWS Service should the company use to distribute the traffic evenly?

explanation.concept: Application Load Balancer distributes traffic across EC2 instances
explanation.correct: An Application Load Balancer sits in front of the three EC2 instances and distributes incoming HTTP/HTTPS traffic across them, which is exactly the horizontal-scaling pattern described.

distractors.A: AWS Global Accelerator improves global network performance by routing traffic over the AWS backbone to the nearest healthy endpoint; it's not the primary tool for distributing traffic across instances within one deployment.
distractors.C: Amazon CloudFront is a content delivery network that caches content at edge locations; it doesn't load-balance traffic across application servers.
distractors.D: Transit VPC is a network hub-and-spoke pattern for connecting multiple VPCs, unrelated to distributing web traffic across instances.

questions.stem: Which of the following approaches will help you eliminate human error and automate the process of creating and updating your AWS environment?

options.B: Use AWS CodeDeploy to build and automate your AWS environment
options.C: Use code to provision and operate your AWS infrastructure
options.D: Migrate all of your applications to a dedicated host

explanation.concept: Infrastructure as Code removes manual, error-prone provisioning
explanation.correct: Using code (e.g. AWS CloudFormation templates) to provision and operate infrastructure makes environment creation repeatable and consistent, eliminating manual configuration mistakes.

distractors.A: Software test automation tools test application code; they don't provision or manage AWS infrastructure.
distractors.B: AWS CodeDeploy automates application code deployments to existing compute, it doesn't provision the underlying infrastructure itself.
distractors.D: Moving to dedicated hosts changes the EC2 tenancy model; it does nothing to automate provisioning or reduce human error.

questions.stem: A company is seeking to better secure its AWS account from unauthorized access. Which of the below options can the customer use to achieve this goal?

options.A: Restrict any API call made through SDKs or CLI
options.B: Create one IAM account for each department in the company (Development, QA, Production), and share it across all staff in that department
options.C: Require Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for all IAM User access

explanation.concept: MFA adds a second factor beyond the password
explanation.correct: Requiring Multi-Factor Authentication for all IAM users means a stolen or guessed password alone isn't enough to sign in, significantly reducing the risk of unauthorized account access.

distractors.A: Restricting all SDK/CLI API calls would break legitimate automation and application access — it doesn't target unauthorized access specifically.
distractors.B: Sharing one IAM account across a department violates least-privilege and destroys individual accountability; it's the opposite of a good security practice.
distractors.D: AWS doesn't support "two login passwords" as an authentication mechanism — MFA using a separate device/app is the actual second factor.

questions.stem: Which AWS Service offers volume discounts based on usage?

explanation.concept: S3 pricing includes volume-tiered discounts
explanation.correct: Amazon S3 Standard storage pricing decreases per GB as usage crosses volume tiers, giving customers a lower effective rate at higher usage levels.

distractors.A: Amazon VPC itself is free to use (you pay for the resources inside it, like NAT gateways); it has no usage-based volume discount structure.
distractors.C: Amazon Lightsail uses simple flat monthly bundle pricing, not a volume discount model.
distractors.D: AWS Cost Explorer is a cost-visualization and reporting tool; it doesn't itself have usage pricing or volume discounts.

questions.stem: Which of the following factors should be considered when determining the region in which AWS Resources will be deployed? (Choose TWO)

options.E: Geographic proximity to the company's location

explanation.concept: Region selection balances compliance and cost against other factors
explanation.correct: Data sovereignty (legal requirements on where data can reside) and cost (pricing varies by Region) are two of the standard criteria AWS documents for choosing a Region, alongside latency, service availability, and compliance requirements.

distractors.A: Security level does not vary by Region — AWS applies the same security standards and shared responsibility model globally.
distractors.D: The number of VPCs planned is an account-level architecture decision, not a factor that drives which Region to deploy into.
distractors.E: Geographic proximity to the company's own location matters far less than proximity to end users/customers, and isn't one of the two best answers here.

questions.stem: You are running a financial services web application on AWS. The application uses a MySQL database to store the data. Which of the following AWS services would improve the performance of your application by allowing you to retrieve information from fast in-memory caches?

explanation.concept: ElastiCache adds an in-memory caching layer in front of a database
explanation.correct: Amazon ElastiCache (Redis or Memcached) is an in-memory data store used as a cache in front of a database like MySQL/RDS, dramatically reducing read latency for frequently accessed data.

distractors.A: Amazon EFS is a managed NFS file system for shared file storage, not an in-memory cache.
distractors.B: Amazon Neptune is a managed graph database service, unrelated to in-memory caching for a MySQL workload.
distractors.D: DAX is specifically an in-memory cache for DynamoDB, not for MySQL-based applications.

questions.stem: What are the advantages of using Auto Scaling Groups for EC2 instances?

options.A: Auto Scaling Groups caches the most recent responses at global edge locations to reduce latency and improve performance
options.B: Auto Scaling Groups scales EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones to increase application availability and fault tolerance
options.C: Auto Scaling Groups scales EC2 instances across multiple regions to reduce latency for global users
options.D: Auto Scaling Groups distributes application traffic across multiple Availability Zones to enhance performance

explanation.concept: Auto Scaling adjusts capacity across AZs for availability
explanation.correct: Auto Scaling Groups can launch instances across multiple Availability Zones and automatically replace unhealthy ones, which increases both application availability and fault tolerance.

distractors.A: Caching responses at edge locations describes Amazon CloudFront, not Auto Scaling.
distractors.C: Auto Scaling Groups operate within a Region across AZs; they don't scale instances across multiple Regions.
distractors.D: Distributing traffic across Availability Zones is the job of an Elastic Load Balancer, not Auto Scaling itself.

questions.stem: The TCO gap between AWS infrastructure and traditional infrastructure has widened over the recent years. Which of the following could be the reason for that?

options.A: AWS helps customers invest more in capital expenditures
options.B: AWS automates all infrastructure operations, so customers save more on human resources costs
options.C: AWS continues to lower the cost of cloud computing for its customers
options.D: AWS secures AWS resources at no additional charge

explanation.concept: AWS passes economies of scale on to customers over time
explanation.correct: AWS has a long track record of repeatedly lowering prices as its own scale and efficiency improve, which widens the TCO advantage over on-premises infrastructure whose costs don't fall the same way.

distractors.A: AWS actually helps customers shift spend from capital expenditure to operating expenditure (pay-as-you-go), the opposite of investing more in capex.
distractors.B: AWS doesn't automate "all" infrastructure operations, and this overstated claim isn't the documented driver of the widening TCO gap.
distractors.D: Security of the cloud is included at no extra charge, but that's a security benefit, not the cost-reduction mechanism behind a widening TCO gap.

questions.stem: Which of the following are examples of the customer’s responsibility to implement “security IN the cloud”? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Building a schema for an application
options.D: Patch management of the underlying infrastructure

explanation.concept: Security IN the cloud is the customer's side of the shared responsibility model
explanation.correct: Building an application's data schema and encrypting the file system are both customer-controlled configuration and data-layer tasks — squarely "security in the cloud," the customer's responsibility.

distractors.B: Replacing physical hardware is an infrastructure task AWS handles as "security of the cloud."
distractors.C: Creating/managing the hypervisor is AWS's responsibility as the underlying virtualization layer.
distractors.D: Patch management of the underlying infrastructure (host OS, hypervisor) is AWS's responsibility, not the customer's.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a type of MFA device that customers can use to protect their AWS resources?

explanation.concept: MFA device types: virtual, hardware token, and U2F security key
explanation.correct: A U2F (Universal 2nd Factor) security key is a physical hardware device customers can register as an MFA device for their AWS account, alongside virtual MFA apps and hardware TOTP tokens.

distractors.A: AWS CloudHSM is a dedicated hardware security module for cryptographic key management, not an MFA device.
distractors.C: AWS Access Keys are long-term credentials for programmatic API access, not an MFA mechanism.
distractors.D: An AWS Key Pair is used for SSH access to EC2 instances, not for multi-factor sign-in authentication.

questions.stem: A company is seeking to deploy an existing .NET application onto AWS as quickly as possible. Which AWS Service should the customer use to achieve this goal?

explanation.concept: Elastic Beanstalk is the fast path to deploy an existing app
explanation.correct: AWS Elastic Beanstalk lets you upload an existing application (including .NET) and automatically handles provisioning, load balancing, scaling, and health monitoring, making it the quickest way to get an app running on AWS without managing infrastructure by hand.

distractors.A: Amazon SNS is a pub/sub messaging service, unrelated to deploying an application.
distractors.C: AWS Systems Manager is an operations/management tool for existing infrastructure, not a rapid application deployment service.
distractors.D: AWS Trusted Advisor gives best-practice recommendations; it doesn't deploy applications.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a factor when estimating the costs of Amazon EC2? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The amount of time the instances will be running

explanation.concept: EC2 cost drivers: compute, IPs, and instance count — not security groups or Route 53 zones
explanation.correct: Security groups and Hosted Zones don't factor into EC2 pricing at all — security groups are free to create/use, and Hosted Zones are a Route 53 (DNS) billing item, unrelated to EC2 cost estimation.

distractors.A: Running time is a direct driver of EC2 compute cost, so it is a relevant factor (not one of the two correct "NOT" answers).
distractors.C: Elastic IP addresses incur charges when allocated but not attached to a running instance, making them a relevant EC2 cost factor.
distractors.E: The number of instances running directly multiplies compute cost, so it is clearly a relevant EC2 cost factor.

questions.stem: Which AWS Service helps enterprises extend their on-premises storage to AWS in a cost-effective manner?

explanation.concept: Storage Gateway bridges on-premises storage to AWS
explanation.correct: AWS Storage Gateway is a hybrid storage service that connects on-premises applications to AWS cloud storage (S3, EBS, or Glacier-backed volumes), letting enterprises extend on-prem storage capacity cost-effectively.

distractors.A: AWS Data Pipeline orchestrates data movement and transformation between compute/storage services; it isn't a hybrid storage extension service.
distractors.C: Amazon Aurora is a managed relational database, unrelated to extending on-premises storage.
distractors.D: Amazon EFS is a cloud-native NFS file system for use by AWS compute resources, not a hybrid on-premises extension tool.

questions.stem: A company is building an online cloud storage platform. They need a storage service that can scale capacity automatically, while minimizing cost. Which AWS storage service should the company use to meet these requirements?

explanation.concept: S3 scales storage automatically with pay-as-you-go pricing
explanation.correct: Amazon S3 is an object storage service that scales capacity automatically with no provisioning required, and customers pay only for what they store — ideal for a storage platform that must grow without manual capacity planning.

distractors.B: Amazon EBS volumes are provisioned with a fixed size that must be manually resized, so it doesn't scale automatically.
distractors.C: Amazon Elastic Container Service runs containers; it is a compute service, not a storage service.
distractors.D: AWS Storage Gateway connects on-premises environments to AWS storage; it's not itself the scalable storage backend for a cloud storage platform.

questions.stem: You have just hired a skilled sys-admin to join your team. As usual, you have created a new IAM user for him to interact with AWS services. On his first day, you ask him to create snapshots of all existing Amazon EBS volumes and save them in a new Amazon S3 bucket. However, the new member reports back that he is unable to create neither EBS snapshots nor S3 buckets. What might prevent him from doing this simple task?

options.A: EBS and S3 are accessible only to the root account owner
options.B: The systems administrator must contact AWS Support first to activate his new IAM account
options.C: There is not enough space in S3 to store the snapshots
options.D: There is a non-explicit deny to all new users

explanation.concept: New IAM users start with no permissions (implicit deny)
explanation.correct: By default, a newly created IAM user has no permissions attached; IAM's default is an implicit deny on everything until a policy explicitly grants access, so he can't touch EBS or S3 until permissions are attached.

distractors.A: EBS and S3 are not restricted to the root account — IAM users can absolutely be granted access to them via policies.
distractors.B: New IAM users are usable immediately after creation; there's no AWS Support activation step required.
distractors.C: S3 storage capacity is effectively unlimited for this purpose; running out of space isn't a real blocker here.

questions.stem: An external auditor is requesting a log of all accesses to the AWS resources in the company’s account. Which of the following services will provide the auditor with the requested information?

explanation.concept: CloudTrail is the audit log of account activity
explanation.correct: AWS CloudTrail records every API call made against the account — who made it, when, and from where — making it the service that supplies an auditor with a full access log.

distractors.B: Amazon CloudFront is a content delivery network; it doesn't log account-wide API access.
distractors.C: AWS CloudFormation provisions infrastructure from templates; it's not an audit logging service.
distractors.D: Amazon CloudWatch monitors metrics, logs, and alarms for operational performance, not a full identity-level audit trail of API calls.

questions.stem: Which of the below options is true of Amazon Cloud Directory?

options.A: Amazon Cloud Directory allows the organization of hierarchies of data across multiple dimensions
options.B: Amazon Cloud Directory enables the analysis of video and data streams in real time
options.C: Amazon Cloud Directory allows users to access AWS with their existing Active Directory credentials
options.D: Amazon Cloud Directory allows for registration and management of domain names

explanation.concept: Amazon Cloud Directory stores hierarchical, multi-dimensional data
explanation.correct: Amazon Cloud Directory is a managed directory service that lets you organize data into flexible, multiple hierarchies (dimensions) at once, unlike a traditional single-hierarchy directory.

distractors.B: Real-time video/data stream analysis describes services like Kinesis Video Streams, not Cloud Directory.
distractors.C: Accessing AWS with existing Active Directory credentials describes AWS Directory Service / AD Connector, a different service.
distractors.D: Domain name registration and management describes Amazon Route 53, not Cloud Directory.

questions.stem: A user has opened a "Production System Down" support case to get help from AWS Support after a production system disruption. What is the expected response time for this type of support case?

explanation.concept: Business/Enterprise Support response times scale with case severity
explanation.correct: A "Production System Down" case is the most severe category under Business and Enterprise Support plans, and AWS commits to a one-hour first response time for it.

distractors.A: 12 hours is the response time for a lower-severity "general guidance" or similar case type, not for a production-down case.
distractors.B: 15 minutes is the response commitment reserved for "business-critical system down" under the Enterprise plan specifically, a different severity tier from the general "production system down" case here.
distractors.C: 24 hours is far too slow for a case marked as a production outage.

questions.stem: Which of the below options is a best practice for making your application on AWS highly available?

options.A: Deploy the application to at least two Availability Zones
options.B: Use Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) across multiple AWS Regions
options.C: Deploy the application code on at least two servers in the same Availability Zone
options.D: Rewrite the application code to handle all incoming requests

explanation.concept: High availability starts with spreading across multiple Availability Zones
explanation.correct: Deploying to at least two Availability Zones is the foundational best practice for high availability, since it protects the application from a single data-center-level failure.

distractors.B: Using ELB across multiple Regions is a much more advanced/costly pattern than the basic best practice being asked about, and Regions aren't the standard first-line HA unit.
distractors.C: Deploying to multiple servers within a single Availability Zone still leaves the application exposed if that one AZ fails.
distractors.D: Rewriting application code doesn't address infrastructure-level availability at all.

questions.stem: Which of the following should be taken into account when performing a TCO analysis regarding the costs of running an application on AWS VS on-premises? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: TCO on-prem vs AWS includes hidden facility and labor costs
explanation.correct: Labor/IT staffing costs and facility overhead like cooling and power consumption are classic on-premises costs that a TCO comparison must include, since AWS eliminates or dramatically reduces them.

distractors.C: "Amazon EBS computing power" isn't a meaningful TCO line item — EBS is storage, not compute, and this phrase doesn't correspond to a real cost category.
distractors.D: Software architecture is a design decision, not itself a cost input for a TCO calculation.
distractors.E: Software compatibility is a technical migration consideration, not a direct cost factor weighed in a TCO analysis.

questions.stem: Your company requires a response time of less than 15 minutes from support interactions about their business-critical systems that are hosted on AWS if those systems go down. Which AWS Support Plan should this company use?

explanation.concept: Enterprise Support offers the fastest response commitment
explanation.correct: AWS Enterprise Support commits to a 15-minute response time for business-critical system down cases, the fastest response tier of any Support plan — matching the requirement described.

distractors.A: Basic Support provides no case response SLA for technical issues beyond account/billing support.
distractors.B: Developer Support offers response times measured in hours (e.g. up to 24 hours), far slower than 15 minutes.
distractors.C: Business Support's fastest response for business-critical issues is one hour, not 15 minutes.

questions.stem: Which of the following AWS offerings are serverless services? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: Serverless means no servers to provision or manage
explanation.correct: AWS Lambda (serverless compute) and Amazon DynamoDB (serverless NoSQL database) both require no server provisioning or management — capacity and scaling are handled automatically by AWS.

distractors.A: Amazon EC2 requires you to provision and manage virtual server instances yourself, the opposite of serverless.
distractors.D: Amazon EMR runs on a managed cluster of EC2 instances that you size and manage, not a serverless offering.
distractors.E: Amazon RDS runs on provisioned database instances you size and manage, not a serverless service by default.

questions.stem: Which AWS service enables you to quickly purchase and deploy SSL/TLS certificates?

explanation.concept: ACM issues and manages SSL/TLS certificates
explanation.correct: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) lets you provision, manage, and deploy public and private SSL/TLS certificates for use with AWS services like ELB and CloudFront, quickly and at no extra cost for public certificates.

distractors.A: Amazon GuardDuty is a threat-detection service that monitors for malicious activity, unrelated to certificate issuance.
distractors.C: Amazon Detective helps investigate security findings by analyzing log data; it doesn't issue certificates.
distractors.D: AWS WAF filters web traffic against rules to block common exploits; it's not a certificate management service.

questions.stem: Which AWS Service provides integration with Chef to automate the configuration of EC2 instances?

explanation.concept: OpsWorks manages configuration via Chef and Puppet
explanation.correct: AWS OpsWorks is a configuration management service that provides managed Chef and Puppet, letting you automate how EC2 instances are configured using Chef recipes/cookbooks.

distractors.A: AWS Config tracks and evaluates resource configuration changes for compliance; it doesn't integrate with Chef to configure instances.
distractors.C: Auto Scaling adjusts the number of running instances based on demand; it doesn't perform Chef-based configuration.
distractors.D: AWS CloudFormation provisions infrastructure from templates (infrastructure as code); it's a different automation model from Chef-based configuration management.

questions.stem: A customer is seeking to store objects in their AWS environment and to make those objects downloadable over the internet. Which AWS Service can be used to accomplish this?

explanation.concept: S3 objects are natively downloadable over the internet
explanation.correct: Amazon S3 stores data as objects in buckets and can serve them directly over HTTP/HTTPS with public or signed URLs, making it the right choice for internet-downloadable object storage.

distractors.A: Amazon EBS volumes are block storage attached to a single EC2 instance; they aren't designed for direct internet downloads.
distractors.B: Amazon EFS is a network file system mounted by EC2 instances; it isn't built for public internet object downloads.
distractors.D: Instance Store is ephemeral, instance-local disk storage that disappears when the instance stops; it has no internet-facing download capability.

questions.stem: Which of the following services can be used to monitor the HTTP and HTTPS requests that are forwarded to Amazon CloudFront?

explanation.concept: CloudWatch monitors CloudFront request metrics
explanation.correct: Amazon CloudWatch collects and displays metrics for CloudFront, including HTTP/HTTPS request counts, error rates, and latency, letting you monitor how requests are being handled.

distractors.A: AWS WAF filters and blocks malicious web requests at CloudFront; it protects traffic rather than monitoring it as a metrics/logging service.
distractors.C: AWS Cloud9 is a cloud-based IDE for writing and debugging code, unrelated to monitoring CloudFront traffic.
distractors.D: AWS CloudTrail logs API calls made against AWS accounts/resources, not the end-user HTTP/HTTPS requests flowing through CloudFront.

questions.stem: A company is migrating a web application to AWS. The application’s compute capacity is continually utilized throughout the year. Which of the below options offers the company the most cost-effective solution?

explanation.concept: Steady, predictable usage favors Reserved Instances
explanation.correct: When compute capacity is continually utilized throughout the year, committing to a Reserved Instance term (1 or 3 years) delivers the largest discount versus On-Demand, since the workload's steady-state nature matches the commitment.

distractors.A: On-Demand pricing is the most expensive per-hour rate and is meant for unpredictable or short-term usage, not continuous year-round workloads.
distractors.B: Dedicated Hosts are priced for full physical server control (often for licensing needs), not the most cost-effective option for a typical continually-used workload.
distractors.C: Spot Instances offer deep discounts but can be interrupted at any time, making them unsuitable for a workload that must run continually.

questions.stem: A company wants to grant a new employee long-term access to manage Amazon DynamoDB databases. Which of the following is a recommended best-practice when granting these permissions?

options.A: Create an IAM role and attach a policy with Amazon DynamoDB access permissions
options.B: Create an IAM role and attach a policy with Administrator access permissions
options.C: Create an IAM user and attach a policy with Amazon DynamoDB access permissions
options.D: Create an IAM user and attach a policy with Administrator access permissions

explanation.concept: Long-term human access uses an IAM user with a scoped policy
explanation.correct: For a person who needs ongoing, long-term access, creating an IAM user and attaching a policy scoped to just DynamoDB access follows least privilege — granting only what's needed, not broad admin rights.

distractors.A: IAM roles are best suited for temporary or delegated access (e.g. for services or federated users), not for a permanent, individual employee's long-term access.
distractors.B: Attaching Administrator access grants far more than DynamoDB permissions, violating least privilege.
distractors.D: Granting an IAM user Administrator access is excessive for a task scoped to managing DynamoDB, violating least privilege.

questions.stem: When granting permissions to applications running on Amazon EC2 instances, which of the following is considered best practice?

options.A: Generate new IAM access keys every time you delegate permissions
options.B: Store the required AWS credentials directly within the application code
options.C: Use temporary security credentials (IAM roles) instead of long-term access keys
options.D: Do nothing; Applications that run on Amazon EC2 instances do not need permission to interact with other AWS services or resources

explanation.concept: EC2 instance permissions should come from IAM roles, not embedded credentials
explanation.correct: Attaching an IAM role to the EC2 instance provides temporary, automatically rotated credentials via the instance metadata service, which is the recommended best practice over hardcoding long-term keys.

distractors.A: Manually generating new access keys for every delegation is operationally heavy and still relies on long-term credentials that must be distributed and rotated by hand.
distractors.B: Hardcoding credentials in application code is a well-known anti-pattern — a security risk if the code is ever exposed or checked into version control.
distractors.D: Applications on EC2 frequently need to call other AWS services (e.g. S3, DynamoDB), so this statement is simply false.

questions.stem: Which of the following will help AWS customers save on costs when migrating their workloads to AWS?

options.A: Use servers instead of managed services
options.B: Use existing third-party software licenses on AWS
options.C: Migrate production workloads to AWS edge locations instead of AWS Regions
options.D: Use AWS Outposts to run all workloads in a cost-optimized environment

explanation.concept: Bring-your-own-license reduces migration cost
explanation.correct: Reusing existing third-party software licenses on AWS (via License Mobility or BYOL programs) avoids paying for new licenses, directly lowering the total cost of migrating workloads.

distractors.A: Using self-managed servers instead of managed services typically increases operational overhead and cost, not savings.
distractors.C: AWS edge locations serve cached content for CDNs; production workloads are not migrated to run on edge locations.
distractors.D: AWS Outposts brings AWS infrastructure on-premises for specific hybrid needs; it's a specialized, often costlier option, not a general cost-saving migration strategy for all workloads.

questions.stem: An organization has a legacy application designed using monolithic-based architecture. Which AWS Service can be used to decouple the components of the application?

explanation.concept: SQS decouples application components with a message queue
explanation.correct: Amazon SQS is a managed message queuing service that lets components of a monolithic application communicate asynchronously through queues instead of direct calls, breaking tight coupling between them.

distractors.B: A Virtual Private Gateway is the VPC-side endpoint for a VPN connection; it's a networking construct, not an application decoupling tool.
distractors.C: AWS Artifact provides compliance reports and agreements; it has nothing to do with application architecture.
distractors.D: Amazon CloudFront is a content delivery network for caching and distributing content, not a mechanism for decoupling application components.

questions.stem: Which of the following can be used to enable the Virtual Multi-Factor Authentication? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: MFA is configured through IAM, using the CLI or console
explanation.correct: Virtual MFA devices are enabled by attaching them to an IAM identity, and this can be done either through IAM directly (console) or via the AWS CLI issuing IAM API calls.

distractors.A: Amazon Connect is a cloud contact center service, unrelated to configuring MFA.
distractors.D: Amazon SNS is a pub/sub notification service; it plays no role in enabling MFA devices.
distractors.E: Amazon VPC is a networking service for isolated virtual networks, unrelated to enabling MFA.

questions.stem: According to best practices, which of the below options is best suited for processing a large number of binary files?

explanation.concept: Horizontal scaling suits parallelizable workloads like binary file processing
explanation.correct: Running many EC2 instances in parallel (horizontal scaling) lets you process a large number of independent binary files concurrently, which scales further and more resiliently than a single bigger instance.

distractors.A: Vertically scaling EC2 instances hits a ceiling on instance size and doesn't parallelize independent file-processing work as effectively.
distractors.B: Running RDS instances in parallel doesn't make sense for processing binary files — RDS is a relational database service, not a compute/processing tool.
distractors.C: Vertically scaling RDS instances is about database capacity, unrelated to processing a batch of binary files.

questions.stem: A company is planning to use Amazon S3 and Amazon CloudFront to distribute its video courses globally. What tool can the company use to estimate the costs of these services?

explanation.concept: AWS Pricing Calculator estimates costs before you deploy
explanation.correct: AWS Pricing Calculator lets you model and estimate the cost of AWS services — like S3 storage and CloudFront distribution — before actually provisioning anything, ideal for upfront cost planning.

distractors.A: AWS Cost Explorer visualizes and analyzes costs you've already incurred; it doesn't estimate costs for a not-yet-built architecture.
distractors.C: AWS Budgets sets alerts against actual or forecasted spend on existing resources; it isn't a pre-deployment cost estimation tool.
distractors.D: The AWS Cost & Usage Report is a detailed historical billing dataset, not a forward-looking cost estimation tool.

questions.stem: What should you do if you see resources, which you don’t remember creating, in the AWS Management Console? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Stop all running services and open an investigation
options.B: Give your root account password to AWS Support so that they can assist in troubleshooting and securing the account
options.C: Check the AWS CloudTrail logs and delete all IAM users that have access to your resources
options.D: Open an investigation and delete any potentially compromised IAM users
options.E: Change your AWS root account password and the passwords of any IAM users

explanation.concept: Responding to a suspected account compromise: investigate and rotate credentials
explanation.correct: Opening an investigation and deleting any compromised IAM users, plus changing the root and IAM user passwords, are AWS's recommended steps to contain and remediate suspicious activity in the account.

distractors.A: Stopping all running services is disruptive and not the recommended first step — targeted investigation and credential rotation come first.
distractors.B: Never share your root account password with anyone, including AWS Support — this is explicitly against AWS security guidance.
distractors.C: Deleting all IAM users indiscriminately (rather than just compromised ones) is overly destructive and not the recommended targeted response.

questions.stem: A key practice when designing solutions on AWS is to minimize dependencies between components so that the failure of a single component does not impact other components. What is this practice called?

explanation.concept: Loose coupling isolates component failures
explanation.correct: Loose coupling is the design principle of minimizing dependencies between components (often via queues or APIs) so that one component's failure doesn't cascade to others.

distractors.A: "Elastic coupling" is not a recognized AWS design principle term.
distractors.C: "Scalable coupling" is not a recognized AWS design principle term.
distractors.D: Tightly coupling is the opposite of the described practice — it means components depend directly on each other, so one failure impacts the rest.

questions.stem: Which AWS Service offers an NFS file system that can be mounted concurrently from multiple EC2 instances?

explanation.concept: EFS is the shared, concurrently-mountable NFS file system
explanation.correct: Amazon Elastic File System provides a managed NFS file system that can be mounted concurrently by many EC2 instances across multiple AZs, ideal for shared file access.

distractors.B: Amazon S3 is object storage accessed via API/HTTP, not mounted as a traditional NFS file system across instances.
distractors.C: Amazon EBS volumes attach to a single EC2 instance at a time (with limited multi-attach exceptions for specific volume types); they are not a general-purpose concurrent NFS solution.
distractors.D: AWS Storage Gateway bridges on-premises environments to AWS storage; it isn't the native concurrently-mountable EC2 file system being described here.

questions.stem: Availability Zones within a Region are connected over low-latency links. Which of the following is a benefit of these links?

options.A: Create private connection to your data center
options.C: Automate the process of provisioning new compute resources
options.D: Make synchronous replication of your data possible

explanation.concept: Low-latency AZ links enable synchronous replication
explanation.correct: The low-latency, high-throughput links between AZs within a Region are fast enough to support synchronous data replication (e.g. RDS Multi-AZ), keeping a standby copy consistently up to date.

distractors.A: Private connections to an on-premises data center are provided by Direct Connect, not by inter-AZ links.
distractors.B: Global high availability spans multiple Regions, which is a separate concept from the low-latency links within a single Region's AZs.
distractors.C: Automating resource provisioning is unrelated to the physical network characteristics between AZs.

questions.stem: Which of the following are true regarding the languages that are supported on AWS Lambda? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Lambda only supports Python and Node.js, but third party plugins are available to convert code in other languages to these formats
options.B: Lambda natively supports a number of programming languages such as Node.js, Python, and Java
options.C: Lambda is AWS’ proprietary programming language for microservices
options.D: Lambda doesn’t support programming languages; it is a serverless compute service
options.E: Lambda can support any programming language using an API

explanation.concept: Lambda has native runtimes plus a custom runtime API for any language
explanation.correct: Lambda natively supports several languages (Node.js, Python, Java, Go, Ruby, .NET, and more) out of the box, and its custom runtime API lets you package and run essentially any programming language beyond the native list.

distractors.A: Lambda supports far more than just Python and Node.js natively, and it doesn't rely on third-party plugins to convert code between languages.
distractors.C: Lambda is not a programming language — it is a serverless compute service that runs code you write in supported languages.
distractors.D: This is false — Lambda explicitly does support numerous programming languages, both natively and via custom runtimes.

questions.stem: What are the capabilities of AWS X-Ray? (Choose TWO)

options.B: Facilitates tracking of user requests to identify application issues
options.D: Deploys applications to Amazon EC2 instances

explanation.concept: X-Ray traces requests to find and fix performance issues
explanation.correct: AWS X-Ray traces requests as they travel through a distributed application, helping developers identify where issues and bottlenecks occur, which in turn helps improve overall application performance.

distractors.A: X-Ray observes and traces existing components; it doesn't automatically decouple or restructure an application's architecture.
distractors.D: X-Ray is a tracing/observability tool, not a deployment service for EC2 instances.
distractors.E: X-Ray is a tracing/observability tool, not a deployment service for on-premises servers.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true regarding the AWS availability zones and edge locations?

options.A: Edge locations are located in separate Availability Zones worldwide to serve global customers
options.B: An availability zone exists within an edge location to distribute content globally with low latency
options.C: An Availability Zone is a geographic location where AWS provides multiple, physically separated and isolated edge locations
options.D: An AWS Availability Zone is an isolated location within an AWS Region, however edge locations are located in multiple cities worldwide

explanation.concept: AZs live inside Regions; edge locations are a separate, much larger network
explanation.correct: An Availability Zone is one or more isolated data centers within an AWS Region. Edge locations are a distinct part of the infrastructure, used by CloudFront to cache content close to users, and there are far more of them, spread across many more cities than there are Regions or AZs.

distractors.A: Edge locations are not located inside Availability Zones — they are a separate global network used for content caching, independent of the Region/AZ structure.
distractors.B: This reverses the relationship. AZs are not contained within edge locations; edge locations exist purely to cache and serve content with low latency.
distractors.C: This description conflates AZ with Region. A Region is the geographic area that contains multiple isolated AZs; it does not itself provide edge locations.

questions.stem: Which features are included in the AWS Business Support Plan? (Choose TWO)

options.B: Access to Cloud Support Engineers via email only during business hours
options.C: Access to the Infrastructure Event Management (IEM) feature for additional fee
options.E: Partial access to the core Trusted Advisor checks

explanation.concept: Business Support: 24x7 engineer access, full Trusted Advisor, IEM at extra cost — but no TAM
explanation.correct: The Business Support plan gives 24x7 phone, email, and chat access to Cloud Support Engineers (A), and it adds Infrastructure Event Management as an optional paid add-on for planning high-risk events (C). A Technical Account Manager is reserved for the Enterprise tiers.

distractors.B: Business Support access is 24x7 across phone, email, and chat, not restricted to email during business hours — that limitation describes the lower Developer plan.
distractors.D: A dedicated Technical Account Manager (TAM) is included starting at Enterprise On-Ramp/Enterprise, not Business.
distractors.E: Business Support includes the full set of Trusted Advisor checks, not a partial subset — partial access describes the Basic/Developer plans.

questions.stem: A company is developing a mobile application and wants to allow users to use their Amazon, Apple, Facebook, or Google identities to authenticate to the application. Which AWS Service should the company use for this purpose?

explanation.concept: Cognito federates external social identities into an app
explanation.correct: Amazon Cognito lets a mobile or web app authenticate users through external identity providers — Amazon, Apple, Facebook, Google, or SAML/OIDC providers — and issues temporary AWS credentials or tokens for the app.

distractors.A: Amazon GuardDuty is a threat detection service that analyzes account activity for malicious behavior; it plays no role in end-user authentication.
distractors.B: Amazon Personalize builds recommendation engines from usage data; it has nothing to do with identity or sign-in.
distractors.D: AWS IAM manages access to AWS resources for users, groups, and roles within an account — it is not designed for federating a mobile app's end users through social identity providers.

questions.stem: Which AWS Service allows customers to create a template that programmatically defines policies and configurations of all AWS resources as code and so that the same template can be reused among multiple projects?

explanation.concept: CloudFormation: infrastructure as reusable code
explanation.correct: AWS CloudFormation lets you define AWS resources and their configuration in a template (JSON or YAML) that can be version-controlled and reused to stand up identical environments across projects or accounts.

distractors.B: AWS Config records and evaluates resource configurations against rules for compliance tracking; it does not provision resources from a template.
distractors.C: AWS CloudTrail logs API calls for auditing; it has no role in defining or provisioning infrastructure.
distractors.D: AWS Auto Scaling adjusts capacity for existing resources based on demand; it does not define infrastructure as a reusable template.

questions.stem: Which of the following are advantages of using AWS as a cloud computing provider? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Eliminates the need to monitor servers and applications
options.B: Manages all the compliance and auditing tasks
options.C: Provides custom hardware to meet any specification
options.D: Eliminates the need to guess on infrastructure capacity needs
options.E: Enables customers to trade their capital expenses for operational expenses

explanation.concept: Cloud benefits: elasticity removes capacity guesswork, and Capex becomes Opex
explanation.correct: AWS removes the need to guess future capacity because you can scale resources up or down as demand changes (D), and it lets you trade large upfront capital investment in hardware for variable operational spending that tracks actual usage (E).

distractors.A: AWS still requires you to monitor your own applications and workloads — AWS operates the underlying infrastructure, but the customer remains responsible for monitoring what runs on it.
distractors.B: Compliance and auditing follow the shared responsibility model — AWS secures the infrastructure, but the customer is still responsible for compliance of what they build and configure in the cloud.
distractors.C: AWS runs on standardized, commodity hardware at massive scale to drive down cost; it does not build custom hardware to each customer's specification.

questions.stem: A customer is planning to migrate their Microsoft SQL Server databases to AWS. Which AWS Services can the customer use to run their Microsoft SQL Server database on AWS? (Choose TWO)

explanation.concept: Running SQL Server means EC2 (self-managed) or RDS (managed) — not a migration or data-movement tool
explanation.correct: You can run Microsoft SQL Server on Amazon EC2 as a self-managed installation, or on Amazon RDS for SQL Server as a fully managed database service where AWS handles patching, backups, and the underlying OS.

distractors.A: AWS Fargate runs containers without managing servers; it is not a platform for hosting a licensed SQL Server database engine.
distractors.D: AWS Database Migration Service moves data between database engines during a migration — it does not host or run the database itself.
distractors.E: AWS Lambda runs short-lived, event-driven functions; it cannot host a persistent SQL Server instance.

questions.stem: Which AWS Service can perform health checks on Amazon EC2 instances?

explanation.concept: Route 53 health checks monitor endpoint availability, not just DNS resolution
explanation.correct: Amazon Route 53 can perform health checks against EC2 instances and other endpoints, monitoring their availability and automatically routing DNS traffic away from unhealthy resources.

distractors.A: AWS CloudFormation provisions and manages infrastructure as code; it does not perform ongoing health checks on running instances.
distractors.C: Amazon Chime is a communications and video conferencing service, unrelated to infrastructure health monitoring.
distractors.D: Amazon Aurora is a managed relational database engine; it does not monitor the health of EC2 instances.

questions.stem: A company is developing an application that will leverage facial recognition to automate photo tagging. Which AWS Service should the company use for facial recognition?

explanation.concept: Rekognition handles image and video analysis, including faces
explanation.correct: Amazon Rekognition provides deep learning-based image and video analysis, including facial detection and recognition, making it the fit for automated photo tagging.

distractors.A: Amazon Comprehend performs natural language processing on text, such as sentiment analysis and entity extraction — it does not analyze images.
distractors.B: AWS IAM manages access permissions to AWS resources; it has no image analysis capability.
distractors.C: Amazon Polly converts text into lifelike speech; it has nothing to do with recognizing faces in images.

questions.stem: Which of the following are examples of AWS-managed databases? (Choose TWO)

options.C: Microsoft SQL Server on Amazon EC2

explanation.concept: Managed database = AWS operates the engine, not just the compute it runs on
explanation.correct: Amazon Neptune is a fully managed graph database, and Amazon RDS for MySQL is a fully managed relational database — in both cases AWS handles provisioning, patching, and backups of the database engine itself.

distractors.B: Amazon CloudSearch is a managed search service, not a database offering.
distractors.C: Running Microsoft SQL Server on EC2 means you install, patch, and administer the database engine yourself — it is self-managed, not AWS-managed.
distractors.D: Running MySQL on EC2 is likewise self-managed: AWS only manages the underlying EC2 instance, not the MySQL engine on top of it.

questions.stem: A company’s AWS workflow requires that it periodically perform large-scale image and video processing jobs. The customer is seeking to minimize cost and has stated that the amount of time it takes to process these jobs is not critical, but that cost minimization is the most important factor in designing the solution. Which EC2 instance class is best suited for this processing?

explanation.concept: Time-flexible workload → Spot Instances for the deepest discount
explanation.correct: EC2 Spot Instances offer the largest discount off On-Demand pricing — up to 90% — in exchange for the possibility of interruption. Since the job's timing is not critical, Spot is the cheapest fit for large-scale, interruption-tolerant batch processing.

distractors.A: On-Demand pricing carries no discount at all; it is priced for flexibility, not for minimizing cost on a workload that can tolerate delay.
distractors.B: Reserved Instances with No Upfront still require a 1- or 3-year capacity commitment, which doesn't fit a periodic job and offers a smaller discount than Spot.
distractors.D: Reserved Instances with All Upfront require the largest upfront commitment and are meant for steady-state, predictable usage — not a workload where timing is flexible and Spot's deeper discount applies.

questions.stem: There is a requirement to grant a DevOps team full administrative access to all resources in an AWS account. Who can grant them these permissions?

explanation.concept: The account owner controls IAM permissions
explanation.correct: The AWS account owner has full control over the account, including granting IAM permissions to users, groups, and roles — such as giving a DevOps team full administrative access.

distractors.B: A Technical Account Manager provides architectural and operational guidance as part of Enterprise Support; they do not grant permissions inside a customer's account.
distractors.C: There is no "AWS security team" with authority over a customer's IAM configuration — permission management is entirely the customer's responsibility.
distractors.D: AWS Cloud Support Engineers help troubleshoot and answer questions through Support cases; they have no ability to grant IAM permissions in a customer account.

questions.stem: You need to migrate a large number of on-premises workloads to AWS. Which AWS service is the most appropriate?

explanation.concept: Server Migration Service moves on-premises VMs into AWS at scale
explanation.correct: AWS Server Migration Service (SMS) is an agentless service purpose-built to migrate large numbers of on-premises virtual machine workloads to AWS as Amazon Machine Images.

distractors.A: There is no such service; S3 Transfer Acceleration speeds up uploads into S3 over the CloudFront network — it does not migrate server workloads.
distractors.C: AWS Database Migration Service is scoped to migrating databases specifically, not general server/VM workloads.
distractors.D: AWS Application Discovery Service inventories and analyzes on-premises servers to help plan a migration; it does not perform the migration itself.

questions.stem: What are some key benefits of using AWS CloudFormation? (Choose TWO)

options.A: It helps AWS customers deploy their applications without worrying about the underlying infrastructure
options.B: It applies advanced IAM security features automatically
options.C: It automates the provisioning and updating of your infrastructure in a safe and controlled manner
options.D: It allows you to model your entire infrastructure in just a text file
options.E: It compiles and builds application code in a timely manner

explanation.concept: CloudFormation: infrastructure modeled as text, provisioned safely and repeatably
explanation.correct: CloudFormation automates provisioning and updates to infrastructure in a controlled, predictable way (C), and it lets you model your entire environment as a text-based template that can be versioned and reused (D).

distractors.A: That description fits a PaaS-style service like Elastic Beanstalk. CloudFormation still requires you to explicitly define the infrastructure you want.
distractors.B: CloudFormation does not automatically apply advanced IAM security — permissions must be explicitly defined by the customer as part of the template or account setup.
distractors.E: Compiling and building application code is the job of a build service like AWS CodeBuild, not CloudFormation.
